active_projects.description: Derive every TM-system theorem the paper cites, and cite derivations rather than derivability. Scope: every schema that the JPL paper (~/Philosophy/Papers/PossibleWorlds/JPL/possible_worlds.tex) presents as a theorem of TM or of an extension (TM_z, TM_d, TM_r) or of BX and its extensions, in sub:Logic, sub:Extension, the Appendix definitions def:BX, def:BX-z, def:BX-d, def:BX-r, def:TMplus, and any footnote. (1) Audit: for each such schema, locate the Lean declaration in this repository and classify it as a direct derivation tree from the axioms, or as obtained through a completeness engine (derivable_of_valid*, Classical.choice over a Derivable proof). Known result of a first pass: Z1 is the only cited theorem routed through completeness (FormalSystem.Metalogic.CompletenessDerived.z1Thm wraps z1Derivable, which applies BXCanonical.derivable_of_validZTime to SoundnessLemmas.z1_valid); DF (DiscreteUnfolding.dfSchema), the discreteness witness (DiscreteUnfolding.succIndicator), CO (DedekindDerived.coDerived), DN (LinearityDerived.density), TC, TL, TK, T4, TF, P1-P4, NP, NF, NA are direct derivation trees. The completeness-route declaration may remain as a cross-check but must no longer be the cited one. Prove the paper's Gluing lemma `app:gluing` in full generality: for any task frame F and convex histories tau1, tau2 over F with domains X1, X2 such that X1 ∩ X2 is nonempty and tau1, tau2 agree on it, the union tau1 ∪ tau2 is the unique convex history over F with domain X1 ∪ X2 restricting to both.

WHAT EXISTS, to reuse rather than rebuild. The repository has two special cases: the closed-interval seam case `Presheaf.sheaf_clause` (FormalSystem/Semantics/Presheaf/Sheaf.lean: sections over [0,l1] and [0,l2] glued at a shared endpoint) and the directed-family case `Presheaf.directed_gluing_clause` (FormalSystem/Semantics/Presheaf/Directed.lean), together with the ray-layer seam gluing landed by task 719 (FormalSystem/Semantics/Presheaf/Ray.lean). None covers two arbitrary convex domains with nonempty overlap. The general lemma is what the paper's convex-history layer actually uses -- the pasting operation rho ⌢_z sigma in the cut proof of cor:deterministic-completeness is an instance -- so it should be stated once at the convex-history layer (PartialHistory / convex domains under FormalSystem/Semantics/Extension/) and the two Presheaf cases either shown to be instances or left independent, by an explicit decision recorded in the docstring.

(2) Choice-freeness: rmk:choice lists app:gluing among the choice-free results, so pin it with #print axioms. (3) Docstrings citing app:gluing.

active_projects.description:
Prove lem:canonical-frames, the four claims the paper makes about its two canonical countermodel frames (def:canonical-frames): (a) the translation frame F^tr_D = (D, D, ⇒), with w ⇒_d u iff u = w + d, is a Deterministic task frame; (b) its possible worlds are exactly the translations sigma_c(z) = z + c for c ∈ D; (c) the two-state frame F^ts_D (W = {w0, w1}, ⇒_0 the identity, every positive duration permitting every transition) is a task frame just in case D is Discrete -- Limit fails whenever D has no least positive duration; (d) when it is, it is not Deterministic and every function D → {w0, w1} is one of its possible worlds.

WHAT EXISTS. FormalSystem/Semantics/Frames/Standard.lean has `translationFrame D : FrameOver D` with `translationFrame_isRegular` for every temporal order and `translationRel_fib_subsingleton` (the singleton-fibre fact behind determinism), and `permissiveFrame D so nm`, built only under `SuccOrder` and `NoMaxOrder` instances, i.e. only for discrete D. FormalSystem/Semantics/Correspondence/DurationFrames.lean has the canonical histories `translationHist` and `permissiveHist D so nm f` for an arbitrary assignment f (already half of (d)), plus the `*_realizes` lemmas. FormalSystem/Metalogic/Independence/RealTranslationFrame.lean has the ℝ instance: `f1_deterministic`, `f1_total_eq_orbit`, `f1_eq_of_states_eq`. None of these states (b), the 'only if' half of (c), or the non-determinism in (d) for a general D.

DELIVER: (b) the set equation H_F = {sigma_c | c ∈ D} for `translationFrame D`, or equivalently an `Equiv` between its world histories and D, over every temporal order; (a) `(translationFrame D).Deterministic`, generalising `f1_deterministic` (or transferred from the ℝ instance if cheaper -- say which); (c) both halves: Limit holds for the permissive relation on Bool when D has a least positive duration and fails otherwise, so the relation is regular iff D is discrete; (d) `¬ (permissiveFrame D so nm).Deterministic`, and that `permissiveHist` is a bijection between assignments D → Bool and world histories. Docstrings cite def:canonical-frames and lem:canonical-frames.

active_projects.description:
Prove prop:archimedean in the generality the paper states it: for every Discrete temporal order D that is not Archimedean, neither Z1 (Future(Future φ → φ) → (future Future φ → Future φ)) nor UZ (future φ → ¬φ U φ) is valid over D. Both countermodels live on the translation frame F^tr_D along sigma_0 and turn on one division of D: the times within finitely many unit steps of 0 and those beyond every multiple of the unit. For Z1, |p| is the complement of the near times; for UZ, |p| is a copy of ℤ sitting above every multiple of 1.

WHAT EXISTS. FormalSystem/Metalogic/Conservativity/Z1Countermodel.lean machine-checks the Z1 failure at the single carrier ℚ ×ₗ ℤ (`not_minus_derivable_z1`, over `multiFamTaskFrameGen`), and FormalSystem/Metalogic/Independence/LexIntWitness.lean has `LexInt.not_archimedean`. FormalSystem/Metalogic/Conservativity.lean's docstring RESTATES the paper's every-non-Archimedean-order claim as prose, but the tree proves no such theorem, and nothing refutes UZ semantically at any non-Archimedean carrier. FormalSystem/Semantics/DurationClassification.lean has `archimedean_of_succ` and the successor-Archimedean normalisation (`ValidDiscrete ↔ ValidInt`, task 475), which is the positive side of the same picture.

DELIVER, over an arbitrary D with a least positive duration (`SuccOrder`) and `¬ Archimedean D`: the two countermodels on `translationFrame D` along `translationHist`, giving `¬ ValidOn (translationFrame D) (Z1 p)` and `¬ ValidOn (translationFrame D) (UZ p)`, hence failure over the Discrete class at every non-Archimedean carrier. Then decide, and record, whether the ℚ ×ₗ ℤ module becomes an instance of the general theorem or stays as the concrete witness; its downstream consumers (`tmMinusCompleteZTime_refuted`, the CEF deliverables) must keep compiling either way.

DEPENDENCY AND TIMING. Depends on task 788, which is re-deriving Z1 from UZ (TM_z = TM + UZ, Z1 derived) and touches Conservativity/Backward.lean and Independence/ZTimeSharpness.lean: wait for it, then state the result against the post-788 names. The paper-side revision (PossibleWorlds task 172) will reword prop:archimedean to match; the semantic countermodels do not care which of UZ and Z1 is primitive.

active_projects.description:
Prove lem:after-negation, and the cut cor:after-negation-stable, for the event operators of def:event-operators. The paper defines in BL: After(φ,ψ) := ¬φ U (φ ∧ ψ); Release(φ,ψ) := ¬(¬φ U ¬ψ); Before(φ,ψ) := Release(ψ,¬φ) ∧ future φ; so After(φ,⊤) = ¬φ U φ says there is a next φ-time. lem:after-negation: After(φ,⊤) → (¬After(φ,ψ) ↔ After(φ,¬ψ)) is valid over every task frame. The proof is that any two next φ-times coincide (the earlier would lie strictly between x and the later), so under the guard After(φ,χ) holds at (tau, x) iff χ holds at the unique next φ-time.

WHAT EXISTS. FormalSystem/Syntax/Formula.lean already defines `next` (⊥ U φ) and `release`; there is no `after` or `before`, and no next-time uniqueness lemma at the semantic layer.

DELIVER: (1) `Formula.after` and `Formula.before` beside `release`, with the paper's equations as simp lemmas and `reflectTime` / `reflect_time_norm` entries if the derived-operator table requires them -- check how `release` is threaded through the `Formula.reflect_time_*` lemmas and the BimodalTools enumerators before adding anything, and do NOT register the new operators with the dataset tooling unless that tooling is updated in the same phase; (2) the semantic uniqueness lemma: if z and z' are both next φ-times after x along tau then z = z'; (3) `after_negation_valid`, the lemma itself, over every task frame; (4) the Stability corollary cor:after-negation-stable -- the same equivalence under the guard with the stability operator prefixed, in both its universal and its existential reading -- which lives in the Plus language (`PlusFormula`, `stab`): decide whether to state it there through the embedding or to leave it as a recorded follow-up, and say which.

PAPER ANCHORS. def:event-operators and lem:after-negation in /home/benjamin/Philosophy/Papers/PossibleWorlds/JPL/possible_worlds.tex; the `% PORT:` comment under lem:after-negation is the marker to clear. cor:after-negation-stable is CUT from the paper and kept verbatim in /home/benjamin/Philosophy/Papers/PossibleWorlds/JPL/appendix_cut_material.tex under the header 'removed by task 169 ... cor:after-negation-stable' -- a specification to implement, not a theorem to cite.

active_projects.description:
Formalize the paper's nomic frames, the frame-level half of the nomic appendix. def:nomic-frame replaces the task relation by a relativized family ⇒^w, one task relation per world state w, each satisfying def:frame, so that F^w := (W, D, ⇒^w) is a task frame; the law-histories H_F^w are the possible worlds of F^w and H_F is their union over w. def:nomic-properties: Lawful (tau ∈ H_F^{tau(x)} for all tau ∈ H_F and x), Static (H_F^{tau(x)} = H_F^{tau(y)} for all tau, x, y), Uniform (H_F^w = H_F for all w). def:nomic-witnesses fixes the ℤ-time presentation by one-step relations R_w with ⇒^w_n = R_w^n and the reflection convention for n < 0.

NOTHING EXISTS. The tree has no nomic frame, no relativized relation and no law-history; FormalSystem/OpenLanguage.lean's docstring lists 'the nomic operator, over a four-place task relation ⇒ʷ indexed by world states' under 'manuscript operators without a formalization'. The operator and its logic are task 795, which depends on this one.

DELIVER: (1) `NomicFrame D`: one carrier W with a family of general frames `at : W → FrameOver D` on it and a regularity hypothesis for each, the law-history sets `lawHist F w` (the world histories of `F.at w`, reindexed to one history type over W) and `H_F` as their union; (2) the three properties as Props, with the trivial implications Uniform → Static and Uniform → Lawful; (3) lem:nomic-occurrence (every state at every time along some law-history at every w) as a wrapper on `PartialHistory.occurrence` at `F.at w`; (4) lem:nomic-recovery: H_F^w = H_F^u iff ⇒^w = ⇒^u, the forward direction through the two-point partial history and `PartialHistory.extension` at F^w exactly as the paper's proof, with `nullity_identity` for d = 0 and the reflection convention for d < 0; (5) prop:nomic-hierarchy's three finite ℤ-time witnesses -- static-not-lawful on {a,b,c}, lawful-not-static on {a,b,e}, static-and-lawful-not-uniform on {a,b,c} -- each assembled from its one-step relations R_w by the ℤ-time scheme (reuse `FrameOver.mem_HF_iff_adjacent` in FormalSystem/Semantics/IntNormalForm.lean for history membership and `TaskFrame.saturation_of_finite` for Saturation), with the independence statements as theorems. OPTIONAL, only if cheap once (4) is in: the cut thm:nomic-primitive, which gives primitive-level forms of Static (a two-point equation on the relativized relation) and Lawful (a three-point condition, with partial-history and ℤ-time finite-path equivalents), kept verbatim in /home/benjamin/Philosophy/Papers/PossibleWorlds/JPL/appendix_cut_material.tex under the header 'moved from appendix ... thm:nomic-primitive'.

active_projects.description:
Formalize the nomic operator and its three results, on the nomic frames of task 794. def:nomic-frame's clause: M, tau, x ⊨ Nomic φ iff M, sigma, x ⊨ φ for all sigma ∈ H_F^{tau(x)}, so the accessibility relation at x relates tau to the law-histories at its current state. prop:nomic-tense-free: over every nomic frame, Nomic φ ↔ □φ holds at every point for every tense-free φ (built from atoms, ⊥, →, □, Nomic), by the same state-set induction as lem:state-set, so every S5 schema for Nomic is valid on that fragment and any refutation needs S or U. thm:nomic-uniform: six equivalent conditions -- transitivity, symmetry, Euclidean (each at one time or at every time), H_F^{tau(x)} = H_F for all tau and x, Uniform, ⇒^w independent of w -- in which case the accessibility relation is H_F × H_F and Nomic φ ↔ □φ is valid for every φ; seriality (D) holds for Nomic over every nomic frame regardless. app:nomic-four: over ℤ-time, Nomic φ → Nomic Nomic φ is valid iff the frame is Uniform, and likewise Nomic φ ↔ □φ, so axiom 4 fails over some Static frame (the static-and-lawful witness of prop:nomic-hierarchy); the refuting sentence is always(¬(p ∧ Next q)) built from a one-step violation of ⇒_1^v along a law-history outside H_F^v.

Teach typst-sync-check.sh Check 1 to resolve namespaced Lean declarations, or rule on the whitelist-vs-docstring convention it currently depends on

MEASURED 2026-10-08. `bash scripts/typst-sync-check.sh` FAILS Check 1 (backtick name resolution) on exactly one finding: VIOLATION `FormalSystem.Semantics.validZTime_iff_validInt` -- "identifier not found in any *.lean file under the Lean source roots", cited from typst/FormalFoundations.typ:790. Three separate implementation dispatches during an /orchestrate run reported it and each correctly declined to repair it as out of scope.

THE CITATION IS CORRECT; THE CHECK CANNOT RESOLVE IT. `theorem validZTime_iff_validInt` is declared at FormalSystem/Semantics/IntTransfer.lean:338, inside `namespace FormalSystem.Semantics` (opened line 70, closed line 353), so the fully-qualified name the manual cites is the right name. Check 1's dotted-identifier branch does a LITERAL grep for the full dotted string and performs no namespace resolution, so a correctly-cited namespaced declaration fails unless its full dotted name happens to appear verbatim somewhere in a .lean file.

WHY THAT IS FRAGILE, measured rather than asserted. Every other fully-qualified FormalSystem.* citation sampled from the typst tree DOES get a literal hit (FormalSystem.Metalogic.BXCanonical, FormalSystem.Metalogic.Conservativity, FormalSystem.Metalogic.Decidability.Compression.decidableValidZTime, FormalSystem.ProofSystem, FormalSystem.ProofSystem.Axioms, FormalSystem.ProofSystem.DerivedAxioms) -- because the name appears in a namespace declaration or a docstring cross-reference, not because the check resolved anything. The manual's citations are therefore validated by coincidence of source text: a correct citation passes or fails depending on whether some docstring mentions it.

THREE ROUTES, none obviously right, to be decided rather than assumed. (1) Teach Check 1 to resolve a dotted name against open namespaces -- correct, but the script is deliberately BUILD-FREE (no lake, no oleans, so it can run in a fast pre-commit gate), so resolution without a build means parsing namespace/end nesting. (2) Whitelist the name in typst/sync-check-whitelist.txt -- the sanctioned escape hatch, BUT it holds 89 entries and ZERO dotted FormalSystem.* entries, and its documented categories are "type-signature / turnstile illustrations" and "typst/template API names (not Lean identifiers)", so a valid-but-unresolvable declaration would set a new precedent and mask a real gap. (3) Change the manual to cite the short name, which does appear literally -- cheapest, but loses the fully-qualified form in a reference manual and does not stop the next namespaced citation from failing.

A FOURTH, if route 1 is rejected: add the fully-qualified cross-reference to IntTransfer.lean's own module docstring, making the citation resolve the same way the other six do. Cost: touching a .lean file changes formalsystem-line-count (347522 at measurement) in typst/generated/status.typ, forcing a status.typ regeneration, and that docstring's existing bullet list uses SHORT names throughout, so a dotted entry would be stylistically inconsistent there.

ACCEPTANCE. Either Check 1 resolves the citation and `bash scripts/typst-sync-check.sh` exits 0, with the chosen mechanism's limits stated where the next citation author will see them; or a recorded verdict naming which route was taken and why the others were rejected, with the finding left visible rather than silently suppressed. If the whitelist route is chosen, say explicitly that it is suppressing a resolution gap and not certifying the name.

NON-GOALS. No change to Check 2 (status.typ counts), Check 2b (module map) or Check 3 (machine appendix). No change to what any generator emits. Do not make the script require a built library -- its build-free property is load-bearing for the pre-commit gate.

BACKLOG RECONCILIATION, verified 2026-10-08 against all 51 open tasks in this repo. No open task covers Check 1 or phantom-citation resolution. Nearest records: 731 (plan-time file_scope harvest must include generated surfaces a .lean edit forces -- adjacent because it also concerns typst-sync-check.sh, but its subject is scope DECLARATION and its NON-GOALS explicitly exclude generator changes) and 741 (agent-system context extensions; mentions typst-sync staleness only as deploy-freshness context). Neither overlaps this.

UPDATE 2026-10-10: THE REPRO ABOVE NO LONGER FIRES; THE MECHANISM GAP IS UNCHANGED.

`scripts/typst-sync-check.sh` now exits 0 (all four checks green). That is NOT because Check 1 learned namespace resolution — it is because the single citation was rewritten at `typst/FormalFoundations.typ:790` from the fully-qualified `FormalSystem.Semantics.validZTime_iff_validInt` to the module-path-plus-leaf form `` `validZTime_iff_validInt` in `Semantics/IntTransfer.lean` ``, which resolves on both halves under the existing rules (the path through the path-exists branch, the bare leaf through the literal grep). Commit: `ci: clear the two standing red gates (PlusRayFibre layer row, stale typst citation)`.

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THIS TASK. The measured finding above is no longer reproducible by running the gate; anyone starting here will see a green gate. The underlying defect is untouched: Check 1's dotted-identifier branch still does a literal grep with no namespace resolution, so any future correctly-cited namespaced declaration will fail the same way unless its full dotted name happens to appear verbatim in a docstring. The sibling citation `FormalSystem.Metalogic.Decidability.Compression.decidableValidZTime`, in the same paragraph, resolves ONLY by that accident — the string appears at `FormalSystem/Metalogic/Decidability.lean:181`. That accidental dependency is the clearest remaining evidence and should be the new starting point.

TO REPRODUCE ON DEMAND: reintroduce any fully-qualified declaration name whose dotted form appears in no `.lean` file, or delete the docstring line at `Decidability.lean:181` and re-run the gate.

THE QUESTION THIS TASK STILL OWNS, now sharpened by having three resolution styles live in one paragraph: decide which citation style the manual is entitled to use, and make the checker honour it. Option (a) teach Check 1 real namespace resolution (match a dotted name against `namespace` prefix plus declared leaf); option (b) rule that the manual cites module-path-plus-leaf and document that, making the two surviving fully-qualified declaration citations non-conforming; option (c) keep the literal grep and accept that fully-qualified citations depend on a docstring mentioning them, which is the status quo and is what made this a recurring finding. Option (c) is the one the evidence argues against.

Run experiment E4: decide StabSaturated on the Bool fixture's mosaic set, and acquire the Hodkinson-Reynolds Handbook sections

WHY THIS EXISTS. Route R2 -- mosaics and quasimodels -- is the rank-2 route to decidability of L+ over discrete time, behind the seam-gluing route R1 and ahead of the closed and low-ranked alternatives. Its amalgamation precondition is already FREE: `paste` glues two mosaics agreeing at a shared germ, choice-free and with uniqueness, exported as `amalgamate` and `amalgamate_unique`. What gates R2 is a single decidability question that the landed probe fixes as a `Prop` and proves only in a degenerate corner, plus two Handbook sections absent from the corpus. The review named this experiment E4 and left it "open for the next round to attack by name". It was never filed.

THE GATE, precisely. `Probe718Mosaic.StabSaturated` is proved only by `stabSaturated_of_sameState` -- the SAME-STATE corner. R2's hypothesis is that `StabSaturated` is decidable on finite mosaic sets with MIXED germ states, under `[F.IsRegular]`, and that a saturated-set existence theorem holds for L+. Neither is established. Re-verify both declaration names against the tree before relying on them; this description's reading is from 2026-10-05.

WHAT TO DELIVER, in two parts.
(1) The probe: decide `StabSaturated` on the two-state Bool fixture's mosaic set at `box-dot(Fp)`, with MIXED germ states rather than the same-state corner. This is the cheapest test of R2's load-bearing hypothesis.
(2) The sources: the Hodkinson-Reynolds Handbook of Modal Logic sections 5.10 and 5.11 bodies are ABSENT from the corpus, which is why R2 cannot be promoted on textual grounds no matter how the probe comes out. Acquire and ingest them. R2's standing cannot be settled by a probe alone.

THE FALSIFIER, which is a valid outcome. A finite mosaic set, with mixed germ states, on which `StabSaturated` is FALSE yet every finite coherence condition holds. That would close R2 the way filtration was closed, and closing a route on evidence is a complete result -- not a failed task. Record it rather than working around it; the no-weakening rule for wired probes applies.

HARD CONSTRAINTS. No complexity claim. Do not file a fourth certificate class on the strength of anything found here: any certificate class presenting finite fibres is already refuted by `Probe710.not_finite_width_fmp`, and R2 is a quasimodel route, not a certificate class. Do not promote R2 above R1 on probe evidence alone; ranking is the review's, and the Handbook sections are part of what any re-ranking would rest on.

LITERATURE. Part (2) is source acquisition; run with `--lit`.

SCHEDULING. Wiring into `scripts/check-evidence-probes.sh` collides with the declared file_scope of tasks 720 and 725, and with the two sibling probe tasks filed alongside this one. Run in a separate cycle from each of them.

ACCEPTANCE. One probe file under `specs/evidence/seam-gluing-ray-product/` compiling under `lake env lean` and wired into `scripts/check-evidence-probes.sh`, whose header states whether `StabSaturated` is decidable on mixed germ states and what that does to R2's standing; plus the two Handbook sections present in the Literature index with an index entry. Either half landing without the other is a [PARTIAL], not a completion.

Evaluate whether the formal:logic implement-phase routing should resolve to a Lean-capable agent when the plan touches .lean files.

EVIDENCE. The formal extension's manifest declares, explicitly and not as a fallback, `routing_agents.implement["formal:logic"] = "general-implementation-agent"` (confirmed by `command-route-agent.sh implement formal:logic`, which resolves `via=noncore-exact`). The task_type `formal:logic` therefore never reaches `lean-implementation-agent`, which the lean extension reserves for `lean4`, `lean4:lake` and `lean4:version`. A formal:logic task whose work is substantially Lean runs without the lean-lsp MCP path, the Lean-specific implementation contracts, and the lake build guidance that a lean4-typed task receives.

OBSERVED CASE. A completed formal:logic task ran its implement phase under general-implementation-agent across seven files, four of them requiring new Lean theorems in `FormalSystem/Metalogic/Decidability/PlusWitnessFamily/Incompleteness.lean`, a `#print axioms` baseline probe in `scripts/check-module-invariants.sh`, scoped and full `lake build` runs, and `lake build BimodalTest`. It completed successfully, so this is a potential improvement rather than a defect report — but it did the Lean work without Lean tooling.

FRAME THIS AS AN EVALUATION, NOT A PREDETERMINED CHANGE. `formal:logic` legitimately covers modal-logic research, proof theory and Kripke-semantics work that touches no Lean at all; the research phase already routes it to `logic-research-agent` rather than `lean-research-agent` for exactly that reason. A blanket reroute of the implement phase to `lean-implementation-agent` would therefore be wrong for part of the population. The question to answer is whether routing should become conditional on the plan's harvested `file_scope` containing `.lean` paths, and if so, where that conditional belongs: in the manifest schema (which today maps task_type to agent name with no predicate), in `command-route-agent.sh`, or in the orchestrator's dispatch composition.

SCOPE. (1) Determine how many non-terminal and recently-completed formal / formal:logic / formal:math / formal:physics tasks declare or harvest `.lean` paths in file_scope, to size the affected population rather than generalizing from one case. (2) Decide among: leave as is and document the rationale; reroute formal:logic wholesale; or introduce a file_scope-conditional routing predicate. (3) If a conditional is chosen, specify where it lives and what it does when file_scope is absent (29 non-terminal tasks currently have no file_scope key at all, so the predicate must have a defined behavior for the unknown case, and must not silently pick the heavier agent on no evidence). (4) Apply the resulting decision in the SOURCE STORE (`~/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/formal/manifest.json` or the routing library), never by hand-patching the deployed `.claude/` tree, then redeploy via `deploy-headless.sh`.

NON-GOALS: no change to research-phase or plan-phase routing, both of which are working as intended; no change to the lean extension's own `lean4*` routing; no new agent definitions.

Add purpose-written `.title` fields to specs/state.json's active_projects entries so TODO.md stops rendering truncated description prose as task names.

CONTEXT: the entry schema (project_number, project_name, status, task_type, description, topic, dependencies, created, last_updated, file_scope) has no title field populated — all 61 entries lack `.title`. This is NOT a defect. `.title` is an optional field with a documented fallback chain: `generate-todo.sh:188` ("Title fallback: derive from project_name if title is empty", `title="${project_name//_/ }"`) and `generate-task-order.sh:192` ("(.title // .description // .project_name) -- a purpose-written .title is preferred over the top of a long prose .description; .description remains the fallback for title-less tasks, and .project_name is the last resort when both are absent"). Effort: small-to-medium, mostly editorial judgment rather than code.

Evaluate removing the TailStable junk-position obstruction at its root by carrying full labels in the sliced certificate. Research report 06_tailstable-backward-conjunct-repair.md established that undischargeable snce positions are determined by the certificate position space posAt, not by the witness family: at target bot-S-bot the closure is {bot S bot, bot} with no state shape, so posAt is the same two-label set for every certificate and LocalCoherentLab forces every label of every certifying family to be empty. Because posAt admits every coherent closure-subset agreeing with slab on state shapes only (atom/box/stab) while temporal obligations are pinned by nothing, carrying FULL labels in the certificate rather than only the state part would make posAt a singleton, so no junk position could exist for either obligation direction and arguably neither liveness filter would be needed. This was option 3 in the repair decision; the chosen repair was option 1 (mirror the filter, landing as TailStableMirror/bwdLiveAt). Option 3 was NOT rejected on the merits, only deferred, because it costs the decidable search that FormalSystem/Metalogic/Decidability/PlusSlicedCertificate/Check.lean is built around, i.e. most of Stage 2 again. Determine whether the obstruction can be removed at the root this way, with refactoring permitted as needed to obtain the best result. The central question is whether decidability of the certificate check survives full labels, and if not, whether a weaker label refinement makes posAt small enough to drop both filters while keeping the search decidable. Compare against the landed option-1 design: with full labels, both TailStableMirror and the forward filter would become deletable and the symmetric two-filter shape in Stable.lean would collapse. Also settle whether the superset failure mode (the Fixture.cert pre-period, repaired by absorption rather than by any filter) likewise disappears under full labels or survives independently.

OPTIONAL, FILED NOT SCHEDULED -- AND LOAD-BEARING AS A CHECK. This task stays unscheduled: status HOLD (user ruling 2026-10-03; prior_status not_started), dependencies [], nothing depends on it. What has changed since it was filed is the claim that "none of the L-plus programme's recommendations rest on it." That is no longer accurate. Its 2EXPTIME lower bound -- ARGUED, not formalized -- is the sanity ceiling that three live records cite against any proposed decision procedure for L-plus. It is load-bearing as a check even while unproved.

ITS ROLE: THE SANITY CEILING. Three records USE this task's argued lower bound as the bound-sanity check -- nothing cheaper than 2EXPTIME is a credible decision procedure. All three were re-verified against the tree on 2026-10-07 (task 738), at their archive locations:

1. specs/archive/718_omega_sequence_decidability_full_lplus/reports/02_ranked-route-analysis.md (archived), the "Complexity sanity check" bullet at line 258: "the CTL* 2EXPTIME-hardness reduction (filed, argued in both directions) is the lower bound; determinization-based upper bounds are doubly exponential, which is consistent. Any proposal cheaper than 2EXPTIME is prima facie wrong. No bound committed."

2. Task 719's description (ray layer, seam gluing and stab fibre; completed and archived at specs/archive/719_ray_layer_seam_gluing_and_stab_fibre, record in specs/archive/state.json -- now provenance rather than a live document), Deliverable 5: "DO NOT LAND A COMPLEXITY CLAIM; the CTL-star 2EXPTIME lower bound is the sanity check on any proposed bound."

3. specs/archive/721_decidability_programme_review_l_and_lplus/reports/01_decidability-programme-review.md (archived) section 3.1 (L-plus routes forward), line 147 -- its Section C ruling on this task is at line 183: "the CTL* 2EXPTIME-hardness argument (task 713, ARGUED) is the lower bound on any proposed procedure; nothing cheaper is credible; no bound is committed here."

ARGUED, NOT FORMALIZED -- AND EVERY CITING RECORD MUST SAY SO. The bound is an argument in prose, not a machine-checked theorem. No Lean declaration establishes it; there is no CTL-star syntax or semantics in the tree to state it against. Every record that cites it must describe it that way, with the ARGUED qualifier attached, exactly as the three records above do. A citation that presents the bound as established, or that drops the qualifier, is a defect in that record.

NO UPPER-BOUND CLAIM MAY LAND FROM THIS TASK. The programme commits to no complexity bound. This task's content is a LOWER bound used as a ceiling: it rules proposals out, it never certifies that any procedure achieves a cost. Deriving or landing an upper-bound claim from it -- in this task's artifacts, in a citing record, or in the write-up -- is a defect, not a result. The asymmetry is the point: a lower bound says "nothing cheaper is credible", it does not say "this much suffices."

GOAL. Raise the 2EXPTIME-hardness of L-plus Z-time validity from ARGUED to MACHINE-CHECKED. The argument is given in both directions in specs/archive/706_lplus_finite_model_property_and_completeness/reports/01_lplus-finite-model-property-research.md section Q4 ("The true order of the state bound"), completing what task 703's round-2 report argued in one direction only -- now archived at specs/archive/703_lplus_compression_and_completeness/reports/02_semantics-first-compression-research.md section 1.6 ("The complexity picture").

THE REDUCTION. Translate CTL-star by A |-> stab and X |-> bottom U ., with non-strict U rendered as e or (g and (g U e)). FORWARD: a rooted total Kripke structure becomes bi-serial by adding one fresh state with a self-loop and an edge to the root, which leaves forward paths from the original states unchanged; stab at (sigma, t) with sigma t = w ranges over histories through w, whose futures are exactly the forward paths from w, and the translation is pure-future so its truth depends only on the future (truth_congr_agreeFrom). BACKWARD: from a Z-model of the translation at (sigma, t), the Kripke structure of the state graph forward-reachable from sigma t satisfies the CTL-star formula at sigma t, by the same two facts read backwards. CTL-star satisfiability is over arbitrary, possibly infinite structures, so no finiteness is needed anywhere.

WHAT IT WOULD BUY. Formalization would turn the ceiling from an argued check into a theorem-backed one: the sharpest available limit on how good ANY certificate class can be. As task 706's Q4 and the archived 703 round-2 section 1.6 record the consequence, with the reduction a theorem no complete certificate class with singly exponential, polynomially checkable certificates could exist for full L-plus without a complexity-theoretic surprise.

CANONICAL WORDING OF THE CONSEQUENCE (quote this, verbatim, in any record that repeats it). L-plus Z-time validity -- equivalently, by negation, L-plus Z-time satisfiability -- is 2EXPTIME-hard by the CTL-star reduction. ARGUED, NOT FORMALIZED: no Lean declaration establishes it. CONSEQUENCE, stated for NON-VALIDITY: if every non-valid formula had a certificate of size singly exponential in the closure size, checkable in time polynomial in the certificate's size, then non-validity (satisfiability of the negation) would be in NEXPTIME and, equivalently, validity would be in co-NEXPTIME; hence 2EXPTIME would be contained in NEXPTIME, equivalently in co-NEXPTIME, since 2EXPTIME is closed under complement. That containment is not refuted but is widely disbelieved. The two class names are the same statement read from opposite sides of the complement: a record may name either, but must say which problem it is placing (NON-VALIDITY with NEXPTIME; VALIDITY with co-NEXPTIME). This is a LOWER bound used as a ceiling: nothing cheaper than 2EXPTIME is credible. It says nothing about any cost sufficing for L-plus and must never be restated as an upper bound. Sources: 706 Q4 (validity / co-NEXPTIME reading) and 703 round-2 section 1.6 (satisfiability / NEXPTIME reading), reconciled 2026-10-07 (task 738): the apparent divergence was one of presentation, not content.

WHAT IT COSTS. A CTL-star syntax and semantics must be added to the tree, which is substantial standalone work the programme otherwise has no need for. Task 706 rates the risk that the reduction has a gap as LOW (its R4) and records it as affecting the complexity picture only.

KEEP-OR-ABANDON IS A PHASE 0 USER RULING, NOT MADE HERE. This revision records the task's role; it does not decide the task's fate and does not schedule it. The decidability-programme review's Section C (specs/archive/721_decidability_programme_review_l_and_lplus/followup-scope-spec.md, Section C at line 220) restates the choice as the user's: keep this as a write-up note, or abandon it. RECOMMENDATION ONLY, not a decision: keep it as a write-up note, because it is load-bearing as a check even while unproved -- abandoning the record would leave the three citing documents pointing at nothing. If the ruling is to abandon, the three citing records need their sanity-check bullets re-sourced to the argument's actual homes (706's Q4 and the archived 703 round-2 section 1.6) rather than to this task.

STANDING (2026-10-03, second re-scope; SUPERSEDES BOTH HEADLINES BELOW). F4 ("finite width implies eventually periodic") is NOT a route and is NOT Phase 2's capstone. Task 718's ranked-route analysis, re-ratified by the programme review in `specs/721_decidability_programme_review_l_and_lplus/followup-scope-spec.md` (Section D, and the "Ranking ratification" section's route R3), DEMOTED F4 from a standalone route to a COMPONENT of route R1 -- the seam-gluing ray product with a universal, complementation-shaped path summary. R3 is its rank in both rankings, described there verbatim as "a COMPONENT, not a route", and "Sequenced under 719". F4 is therefore R1's SUMMARY STEP, sequenced UNDER the gluing route (task 719), and is not attempted before 719's keystone promotion lands. `specs/ROADMAP.md` Phase 2's earlier framing of this task as "the phase's substance and the only item that is open mathematics" and "the one real theorem on this front", and this task's own previous re-scoped headline, both PREDATE that demotion and overstate its standing; the ROADMAP now carries the correction conditionally ("709 if Section D is adopted"; "under the gluing route, after 719 (Section D); not Phase 2's capstone").

DEPENDENCIES. [703, 710, 719]. 719 (ray layer, seam gluing and stab fibre) is added by this revision because F4 is a step inside the route 719 promotes: the summary device F4 would supply is R1's, and which device R1 needs is decided by 719's Deliverable 5 (the decidable-check connection) and by probe E3, not here. 703 and 710 are retained unchanged.

PREMISE REFUTED FOR COMPLETE CLASSES. F4's premise -- finite width -- is refuted for any COMPLETE certificate class by `Probe710.not_finite_width_fmp` (machine-checked, sorry-free, axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], in `specs/archive/710_sliced_class_incompleteness_characterization/probes/NoFiniteWidthModel.lean`, with `#print axioms` at the file's foot). Companions in the same file: `no_finite_width_sat`, `not_certifies`, `not_sliced_complete`, and the positive half `not_plusValidZTime_neg_Φ` -- NOTE the declaration is spelled with the Greek capital (`_Φ`), not `_Phi`. The witness is `Φ := (A' ∧ C') ∧ D` with `A' := □(p ∨ ⊡Fp ∨ ⊡Pp)`, `C' := □(p → ⊡¬Pp)` (together task 706's `θ'`), and `D := □(⊡Fp → ¬⊡¬Xp)`; the obstruction is EXACTLY FINITE WIDTH (limit closure plus finite per-time fibres contradicts König), and it bites already inside the CTL-like fragment this task targets. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE STATEMENT: no surviving form of F4 may be stated for a complete class or for the fragment at large. Any statement that survives MUST NAME THE RESTRICTED FRAGMENT (or the restricted class of structures) it holds for, and must say in its docstring why `not_finite_width_fmp` does not refute it.

TWO OUTCOMES, BOTH HONOURABLE. R1's summary step resolves one of two ways, and which way is R1's decision, not this task's:

Formalize the duration monoid `BD+`, its twisted-arrow category, and `lem:interval-twisted-arrow`: `BD+` is factorization-linear and `Tw(BD+)` is isomorphic to the interval category `Int(D)` by an isomorphism carrying the Johnstone coverage of the one to that of the other.

WHY THIS IS NOW ITS OWN TASK. Task 563 carries this as "OPTIONAL, only if cheap". It is being promoted because the paper has changed around it: the presheaf appendix `app:Structure` was cut from /home/benjamin/Philosophy/Papers/PossibleWorlds/JPL/possible_worlds.tex, and the main-body conclusion is being rewritten to assert the Johnstone route in prose -- interval site, sheaf condition, discrete Conduche fibrations, path category -- with the supporting results promised elsewhere. The lemma is no longer an optional extra on the interval-site task; it is the load-bearing step behind a claim the paper now makes in its body with no appendix under it.

DELIVER:
- The duration monoid `BD+`: the one-object category whose morphisms are the durations in the positive cone, composing by addition with identity 0.
- The factorization category `Fact(l)` of a duration: objects the factorizations `l = x + y` with `x, y` positive, morphisms `(x, y) -> (x', y')` the durations `z` with `z + x = x'` and `y = z + y'`.
- Factorization-linearity: each factorization category is a linear preorder -- any two objects related by at most one morphism, and by at least one in one direction or the other.
- The twisted-arrow category `Tw(BD+)`: objects the durations, morphisms `l' -> l` the pairs `(p, q)` of positive durations with `p + l' + q = l`, composing `(p, q) . (p', q') = (p + p', q' + q)` with identities `(0, 0)`.
- The Johnstone coverage on both `Tw(BD+)` and `Int(D)`, and the coverage-preserving isomorphism `Int(D) iso Tw(BD+)`.

SHAPE OF THE WORK. This is pure order algebra over the positive cone of a linearly ordered abelian group. It needs no task frame, no world states, and no history theory -- only `TemporalOrder.lean`'s carrier and its order and group structure. That makes it the most self-contained item on the categorical front and a reasonable one to land early.

DESIGN DECISION TO RECORD EXPLICITLY, not to settle by accident in the first proof: whether these categories are stated as concrete Lean structures with hand-rolled composition lemmas, or as `Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Category` instances. `grep -rl CategoryTheory FormalSystem/` currently returns exactly one file, `FormalSystem/Boneyard/RetiredTactics/AesopRuleSet.lean`, so the live tree imports no category theory at all. Introducing it is a real dependency decision for the whole categorical cluster (tasks 563-567 included) and should be made once, here, and written into the module docstring with its reasoning -- not made implicitly by whichever task gets there first. The concrete route is cheaper and keeps the import surface flat; the Mathlib route is what makes `fact:conduche-equivalence` and the free-category statement expressible without re-inventing vocabulary. State the trade-off, pick one, say why.

Add time addition operator (+) to the bimodal logic TM. φ + ψ is true at (τ, x) iff ∃ y,z with x = y+z, φ true at (τ,y), ψ true at (τ,z). This internalizes the AddCommGroup structure of D into the object language, extending expressive power from FO[<] to FO[<,+] (Presburger arithmetic). Related to arrow logic (Venema), relevant logic (Routley-Meyer ternary frames), and separation logic (BI). Phase 1: add tadd/tsub constructors to Formula, truth clause in semantics. Phase 2: basic axioms (associativity, commutativity, identity, inverse). Phase 3: soundness proofs. Phase 4: interaction with G/H/U/S/□. Completeness (ternary canonical model) and decidability are open research problems — defer to later phases.

Add topological open set (interior) operator for dense and continuous temporal frames. On discrete ℤ the interior is trivial (discrete topology), but on dense ℚ and continuous ℝ it captures neighborhood-stable truth: Int(φ) true at t iff φ holds in an open neighborhood of t. Related to Dynamic Topological Logic (Kremer-Mints 2005), McKinsey-Tarski topological semantics for S4, and Fernandez-Duque intuitionistic temporal logic. Phase 1: add TopologicalSpace instance to TaskFrame for dense/continuous cases. Phase 2: add interior constructor to Formula with truth clause. Phase 3: axioms (S4-like: Int(φ)→φ, Int(φ)→Int(Int(φ))). Phase 4: interaction with temporal operators and S5 □. Note: DTL is not finitely axiomatizable (Fernandez-Duque 2014) — completeness may require non-standard techniques.

Rank the work accordingly -- this is a four-class uniformity result and a tableau-correctness result, not a race to a first theorem.

The siblings `isTautology_sound`, `isContradiction_sound`, `not_isSatisfiable_sound`, `decide_isValid_sound`, `decideBlocking_isValid_sound` and `decideAuto_isValid_sound` all factor through `sound_of_isValid`.       `exact Classical.em (⊨ φ)`. That is excluded middle for an arbitrary proposition. It
      holds of any predicate whatsoever and says nothing about `⊨` in particular, about
      tableaux, or about computation. It produces no procedure and no `Decidable` instance.
  (ii) `validity_has_decision_procedure (φ : Formula) : ∃ decision : Bool, decision = true ↔ ⊨ φ`

That section also records what is still owed and why it is deliberately not stated there: the completeness direction, hence the biconditional and the four `Decidable (⊨ φ)` instances, needs the fuel/termination side and the truth-lemma gate on top of the landed rule half, and must additionally account for the two rules scheduled outside `allRulesForFC`. AIM (revised 2026-09-18; this paragraph governs everything below). Present the most natural proof system containing the stability modal ⊡ and prove it sound and COMPLETE over the paper's task semantics, at Base and at each extension class (Dense, ZTime, RTime). The logic does NOT need to express state recurrence. The SEMANTICS IS FIXED: task frames with all four frame axioms (Compositionality, Seriality, Limit, Saturation), H_F = ALL total histories, □ over H_F, ⊡ over the histories through the current world state at the current time (PlusTruthAt). Everything else is open to change: new axiom schemata, new inference rules, and extensions of the OBJECT LANGUAGE where completeness takes them. Completeness of the CURRENT PlusAxiom set was never the goal and is refuted; do not re-investigate it. A bundled semantics (□/⊡ over a chosen paste- and shift-closed bundle) is a DIFFERENT semantics: admissible only as an intermediate tool (soundness vehicle, stepping stone), never as the result (see USER DECISION).

ESTABLISHED -- read reports 01-04 and probes 01-04 of this task, and the reports of 624, 625 and 628, first; do not redo. Labels: compiled-mirror = sorry-free Mathlib-only probe mirroring PlusTruthAt (probes 01-03 over ℤ, probe 04 over any ordered abelian group D); compiled-live = `lake env lean` against the repository; paper; UNVERIFIED; recalled.
(a) Current TM⁺ is incomplete at ZTime: LC⁺ := (⟐Xp ∧ ⊡G(p → ⟐Xp)) → ⟐Gp is ℤ-valid and refuted in a paste-closed coarsened-state model (report 01, compiled-mirror). This answers negatively the manuscript's commented-out remark (3832) that TM⁺ completeness "remains open".
(b) Incomplete at Base: BLC := (⟐Fp ∧ ⊡G(p → ⟐Fp)) → ⟐(Fp ∧ G(p → Fp)) is Base-valid by Zorn + `extension` (paper, report 02 §2) and refuted in a compiled coarsened countermodel on ℤ-frame `eR` (Saturation on paper). Dense/RTime non-derivability needs a dense saturated countermodel: 624 removes the Limit obligation (product/colourClock); Saturation of the ordinal-budget colour structure and a .Dense form of paste-closed soundness remain UNVERIFIED (624 §4.1).
(c) Mechanism, restated natively (report 04 §4.1, paper): for a translation- and paste-closed bundle H, the all-histories set of the frame read off H is the topological closure of H in W^D. All-histories semantics = closed bundles; PS/US give paste-closure, MF translation-closure, nothing gives closedness. Saturation supplies the Extension property at infinite W; it is idle at ZTime (oriented-forest argument, report 03 §1.2, paper). Whether Saturation adds any L⁺-validity at the other classes is OPEN.
(d) Soundness vehicle for non-derivability: paste-closed coarsened-state models (Metalogic/Independence/CoarsenedModels.lean plus PS/US arms); compatible with the translation product (624: liftK, c_invariance, pasteClosed_liftK, c_refuted_lift, compiled-live).
(e) Naming. 535's time-naming candidate is unsound (□ sees every shift). Sound and demoted to proof devices: Gabbay IRR (irr_sound) and the ⊡-local clock rule (clock_irr_sound), compiled-mirror over ℤ. Naming rule of record: the STATE-naming rule "from ⊢ (q ∧ ⋀_ψ NOM_q(ψ)) → φ, q fresh, infer ⊢ φ", NOM_q(ψ) := (⟐ψ → □(q → ⟐ψ)) ∧ (⊡ψ → □(q → ⊡ψ)), sound frame by frame at every D with no frame axiom (state_name_sound, compiled-mirror) and also on translation-closed bundles (paper), so it derives no LC_n. It needs no language extension.
(f) The bundled-vs-completion indistinguishability route is closed. All four landed completeness engines build deterministic, linear countermodels (⊡ = id) and none applies as is; states must not be MCSs (that forces Determined).
(g) What ⊡ is. ⊡-truth is a function of the present world state alone (stab_state_only, compiled-mirror at every D; landed as Semantics.stab_state_only). ⊡ is the manuscript's ⟨τ⟩_x modality, not Ockhamist historical necessity (that is ▷): HN fails for ⊡ (hn_stab_refuted, compiled-mirror; compiled-live on F3 := FrameOver.ofStep of the three-state sink relation, proposed name sinkFrame, 625 probe 01) and holds for the open-future modality over AgreeUpTo (hn_open_pure, hn_open_mixed, 625, compiled-live semantic form). FrameOver.rev (time reversal, all four axioms, rev_rev by rfl, agreeUpTo_rev) is compiled-live (625 probe 02). Hence the Reynolds-2003 engine does not transfer beyond its LC ingredient. Invariances: truth is preserved by surjective two-way bounded morphisms (tw_invariance, compiled-mirror ℤ) and by re-timing each history by an order automorphism (repar_invariance, compiled-mirror every D), so L⁺ is blind to durations.
(h) Translation product, 624 (compiled-live). F × D is a task frame at all six FrameOver fields and every class tag (prodFrame, prodFrame_sat; Saturation transfer prodRel_saturation and converse saturation_of_prodRel; Limit from ⇒₀ ⊆ id, prodRel_limit). Validity of L, L⁺ and L⋆ over a class equals validity over its recurrence-free members (validIn_iff_recurrenceFree, plusValidIn_iff_recurrenceFree, starValidIn_iff_recurrenceFree; star_invariance settles report 04 §3.3.3 for L⋆). Canonical frames may therefore be built clocked WLOG. Limit contributes no validity beyond reflexivity of the zero task (TD_zeroFix, zeroFix_limit_clocked, 624 probe 02, compiled-mirror). Any finite reflective serial compositional colour relation with ⇒₀ ⊆ id clocks to a task frame over any D (colourClock): frame axioms are NOT the obstacle at any class -- the truth lemma over ALL histories is. Frame-by-frame validity does NOT transfer to the product (frame_validity_not_reflected); the device never refutes anything F does not and is silent on closure, Saturation, and naming.
(i) Truth lemma, stated natively (report 04 §4.2, paper): with states = ⊡-theories and a translation-closed family 𝒞 of perfectly coherent chronicles, the truth lemma holds iff every trace in the closure of the canonical bundle is the state trace of a coherent chronicle. Failure mode: a trace postponing an inevitability ⊡Fα forever; cure by LC_n in the logic and progress measures carried in the state.
(j) Limit closure. LC_n := ⊡G≤ ⋀_{i<n}(⟐αᵢ → ⟐F⟐α_{i+1 mod n}) → ⟐G≤ ⋀_{i<n}(⟐αᵢ → F⟐α_{i+1 mod n}) is valid at ZTime for all n ≥ 1 and arbitrary αᵢ (lcN_valid_full, compiled-mirror via omega_chain) and at Base by Zorn + `extension` (paper, UNVERIFIED in Lean). LC_n is an instance of LC_m when n ∣ m; LC_1(p) is independent of current TM⁺ (paper); BLC ≈ LC_1. LCU (X-free until-form of Reynolds 2001's LC) is ZTime-only: semantic core compiled-mirror, formula level UNVERIFIED; invalid at Dense/RTime by a Zeno pattern (sketch, UNVERIFIED). The Dense/RTime until-form principle is unknown.
(k) Axiomatizability. ZTime validities are decidable (report 03 §1.3, paper; rests on recalled Rabin; finite model property not established). Base, Dense, RTime: r.e. status OPEN, obstruction located (tree-like preimages need a relative Saturation; MSO over ℝ undecidable, recalled).
(l) Language extensions, 628 (compiled-live). A state-identity test across two times of one history is the minimal resource making recurrence visible (one state register: recF_defines, bindRec_defines, transF_valid); state nominals, registers and propositional quantifiers are needed only to EXPRESS recurrence, which is not a goal. A NAME rule for state nominals gives the ⊡-existence lemma free in a named canonical model (paper) but does not touch closure of the canonical bundle; once nominals enter, class validity ≠ recurrence-free validity, so any WLOG-clocking must precede them. Whether ANY naming rule is needed for the nominal-free system stays OPEN.
(m) AA rule: forward-cone unravelling (aa_expand, cone_twoWay, compiled-mirror) is a ZTime proof device only; formula-level rule UNVERIFIED.

QUESTIONS FOR THE NEXT ROUND, in priority order, each with a verdict and machine-checked evidence wherever checkable.
(P1) AXIOMATIZABILITY FIRST. Are the ⊡-validities r.e. at Base, and at Dense/RTime? Bound this before any engine work: give a proof, a reduction to a held decidability/r.e. result, or a located obstruction. (P2) ZTIME TRUTH LEMMA for TM⁺_Z + LC_n + LCU + the state-naming rule. Design the replacement for Reynolds 2001's one-sided, rooted automaton: emergent histories are limits of splices in BOTH directions, formulas contain S, and there is no root. Use colourClock for the frame side.
(P3) ECONOMY. Does a finite subfamily of LC_n suffice (single-schema candidates), per class? Can the naming rule be dropped entirely -- assess the rule-free route of Di Maio-Zanardo only through held sources (not held: say so)?
(P4) LEAN CHECK of LC_n validity at Base (Zorn over partial histories + `extension`), as a sorry-free probe; ideally via a general "maximal non-erring partial history" lemma reusable by 560.
Bundled completeness is NOT to be researched unless P1 returns a NEGATIVE verdict (see USER DECISION).
BASELINES any candidate must meet: soundness over all task frames of the class, one lemma per new constructor; collapse to the deterministic completeness of 537 under Determined; both directions of conservativity over TM (forward_plus, plusDerivable_ofFormula_iff) re-checked. Settled and not to be reopened: class order (ZTime first, Base second, Dense/RTime last); frame-axiom obligations (h).

USER DECISION (2026-09-19): the Henkin-style (bundled) presentation is REJECTED as cheap -- it buys completeness by changing the semantics, as Henkin models do for second-order logic. The goal is completeness over the standard all-histories semantics. Bundles are to be revisited ONLY if it is PROVEN that no complete system exists for the standard semantics at a class, i.e. its ⊡-validities are not r.e. (P1 negative, with a proof, not a located obstruction). Incompleteness of the current TM⁺ (items a-b) does NOT count: it refutes one axiom set, not every r.e. system.

In the sub-index (specs/literature-index.json): reynolds_2001 (CTL*: LC, AA rule, automaton completeness proof); reynolds_2003_priors-ockhamist-logic-historical-necessity (infinite LC schema, IRR, hues and colours; extended abstract whose completeness proof is a SKETCH; OCR FORMULAS UNRELIABLE -- re-derive from prose, cross-check reynolds_2002); reynolds_2002_axioms_for_branching_time; emerson_and_halpern_-_1986_-_sometimes_and_not_never_revisited_on_branching_versus_linear_time_temporal_logic (fusion/suffix/limit closure); rumberg-zanardo-2019-transition-structures; thomason_1984 (§4: T×W, Kamp frames); thomason-1970-indeterminist-time; burgess_1982_i, burgess_1984_*, gabbay_1994_* (chronicles, S/U, IRR). OPEN RESEARCH QUESTION, not an implementation task. Is the logic of C3 -- the domain-restricted consequence relation -- equal to Burgess-Xu without the unboundedness assumption, plus S5?

WHAT IS ALREADY ESTABLISHED (`specs/553_decide_convex_history_layer_collapse/reports/01_convex-correlate-and-consequence.md` section 4.2) is the CONTAINMENT: C3 includes classical propositional logic, S5 for box, the whole Burgess-Xu monotonicity, enrichment, accumulation, absorption and linearity block, and `modal_future`; and C3 excludes seriality and the uniformity layer. THE FIRST OBSTACLE, which any canonical-model construction will hit immediately (`specs/553_decide_convex_history_layer_collapse/reports/01_convex-correlate-and-consequence.md` section 4.3): the germ constraint. Every C3-validity holds at every one-point germ, and `box (phi U psi)` and `box (phi S psi)` are C3-UNSATISFIABLE for every `phi` and `psi`. That is stronger than the loss of seriality: it constrains what any axiomatization of C3 could look like, since no boxed binary-tense formula can ever be a theorem. active_projects.title: conclusion stage drops null-resolution issue-log entries
active_projects.description:
Close the contract gap that makes null-resolution issue-log entries invisible to the conclusion stage

THE CONCLUSION STAGE SILENTLY DROPS NULL-RESOLUTION ISSUE-LOG ENTRIES. `context/formats/issue-log.md` declares the `resolution` field optional and nullable (its field table row reads "no (nullable)", closed vocabulary `fixed_inline | worked_around | open`). `context/contracts/conclusion-stage.md`'s "The Filter Predicate" admits an entry into channel classification ONLY when `resolution` is `open` or `worked_around`. An entry written with `resolution: null` is therefore neither closed (`fixed_inline`, which legitimately generates no channel item) nor classified -- it reaches NO channel and is invisible to the user. Both documents are internally consistent; the gap is between them.

VERIFIED LIVE, NOT HYPOTHESIZED. `specs/749_c_bound_half_model_a_presentation_size/issues.jsonl` holds 11 entries, every one with `resolution: null` and `suggested_channel: null`. `bash .claude/scripts/orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh --aggregate --session <sid> --tasks 749` returned `proposals: 0`, `wins: 4`, `unknown_classes: 6`. Of the 11 entries, 7 are `kind: "issue"` and were all dropped: six at `severity: minor` (classes `stale-citation`, `plan-deviation`, `plan-gap`, `plan-gap`, `plan-gap`, `build-failure`) and one at `severity: costly` (class `plan-deviation`). The 4 `kind: "win"` entries surfaced correctly, which confirms the aggregator is behaving exactly as written -- this is a contract mismatch, not an aggregator bug. Re-derive these counts from the live log rather than trusting them; they are a snapshot.

DECIDE AND LAND ONE OF THREE. (a) Make `resolution` REQUIRED at write time in `scripts/issue-record.sh`, so an entry cannot be recorded without one -- closes the hole at the writer, but every existing null-resolution entry across the repo stays invisible. (b) Widen the Filter Predicate to treat null-or-absent `resolution` as `open` -- the conservative reading, since an issue recorded without a resolution is an unresolved one; note this alone would have pushed 7 entries from ONE task into channel classification, so weigh proposal volume before choosing it. (c) Keep both contracts as they are and have the conclusion stage report a separate "unclassifiable (no resolution)" tally beside its unknown-class tally, so the entries are at least visible rather than dropped. Options (a) and (c) are composable; (b) subsumes neither. Whichever is chosen, the two documents MUST end up agreeing in writing -- the acceptance condition for this record is that a reader of either file can predict the other's behavior.

ALSO IN SCOPE. `suggested_channel` was null on all 7 dropped entries too. `conclusion-stage.md`'s "The Hint-Versus-Decision Rule" treats that field as a hint the orchestrator may override visibly, which presumes a hint exists; decide whether a null hint is acceptable or whether the writer should require one, and say so in the same place the `resolution` decision is recorded.

SOURCE-STORE BOUNDARY. All four file_scope paths live in a deployed, regenerated tree -- a hand edit under `.claude/**` is wiped by the next deploy and the edit will appear to succeed while having no lasting effect. Implementation MUST resolve `source_dir` from `<project-root>/.claude-extensions.json` for the owning extension (`core`, whose source store is `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core`) and edit at the mirroring paths there, per `.claude/rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md`, then redeploy via `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` and confirm `RESULT=landed_verify_clean`. DELIVERABLE HYGIENE. The edited files are not under `specs/**`, so the prose must carry no task-number references and no record-versioning language; cite durable anchors (file names, section headings, field names) only.

RELATED RECORDS, FOR ORIENTATION AND NOT AS DEPENDENCY EDGES. The roadmap-generator record covering `roadmap-integration.sh`'s partial-write behavior is the sibling core-extension defect with the same source-store boundary, and the file_scope-declaration-hygiene record covers a different blindness in the same admission machinery. No dependency edge to either -- nothing here blocks on them.

Re-pin `lem:nullity` in the paper definitions of record after the JPL paper strengthened it from an implication to a biconditional, and correct the in-tree docstrings that quote the retired wording verbatim.

THE DRIFT. `scripts/check-paper-definitions.sh` reports exactly one drifted anchor against `docs/reference/paper-definitions-of-record.md`:

  OLD (pinned, sha256 94ed018343635a8ef6671daef07eaa72da1cb49fd11043fb3aa9b391a2c9c973):
    $w \Rightarrow_0 w$ for every world state $w \in W$ in every task frame $\F = \tuple{W, \D, \Rightarrow}$.
  NEW (live paper, sha256 8442e2bf6b5f6515f2f906132bbe15fe919973d82ae573dba29a919ad14636f5):
    $w \Rightarrow_0 u$ if and only if $w = u$, for all world states $w, u \in W$ in any task frame $\F$.

The new statement is strictly STRONGER: an implication became a biconditional characterising `⇒₀` as the identity relation.

THE FORMALIZATION IS NOT BEHIND THE PAPER. This is the load-bearing fact for scoping, and it is verified, not assumed: the tree already carries BOTH forms. `FormalSystem/Semantics.lean:257` names them together — the field `FrameOver.nullity` (the weak loop) and the biconditional `FrameOver.nullity_identity`. `FormalSystem/Semantics/IntNormalForm.lean:24` already describes `⇒₀` as the identity and cites `FrameOver.nullity_identity` as the derived theorem for it, and `IntNormalForm.lean:200` discharges a base case with `F.nullity_identity w u`. So no new Lean proof is required by this drift; the record is simply stale relative to a paper the library already over-satisfies.

NOT A CI FAILURE. `check-paper-definitions.sh`'s own usage block documents that an absent paper file is a neutral skip with exit 0, and names that as the CI path, since CI cannot see the paper's repository — confirmed by running it with a nonexistent `--paper`. The gate is red only on a machine where the paper is checked out alongside this repo. It is therefore a local-correctness obligation, not a release blocker.

SCOPE. (1) Re-pin the `lem:nullity` block and its sha256 in `docs/reference/paper-definitions-of-record.md`, following that file's own dated drift-correction convention for an amendment to a decision the record owns; `check-paper-definitions.sh --resolve` is the sanctioned way to obtain the new text and hash rather than transcribing by hand (there is no `--fix` mode, by design). (2) Correct the in-tree sites that quote the RETIRED wording. Four of them label the quotation "verbatim" and so become false on re-pin: `FormalSystem/Semantics/TaskFrame.lean:113` and `:919`, `FormalSystem/Semantics/FrameAxioms.lean:65`, `FormalSystem/Semantics/Extension/Admissible.lean:34`. (3) Review the sites that paraphrase the weak form without claiming verbatim quotation and decide case by case whether each should now cite the biconditional: `FormalSystem/Semantics.lean:255`, `FormalSystem/Semantics/Presheaf/Behavior.lean:91`, `FormalSystem/Semantics/FrameAxioms.lean:113`, `FormalSystem/Semantics/Extension/Admissible.lean:117`, `FormalSystem/Semantics/Extension/Extension.lean:171`, `docs/reference/state-topology-appendix-support.md:103`. Several are legitimate as they stand — a proof that needs only the weak loop should keep citing the weak loop — so this step is a judgment pass, not a search-and-replace. (4) Preserve the record's standing claim that Nullity is DERIVED and not an axiom (`paper-definitions-of-record.md:976`, `TaskFrame.lean:113`): the strengthening does not promote it to an axiom.

ACCEPTANCE. `scripts/check-paper-definitions.sh` exits 0 against the live paper; `lake build` green; `scripts/readme-lint.sh` and `scripts/check-module-invariants.sh --no-build` still exit 0; no docstring claims a verbatim quotation it does not reproduce.

NON-GOALS: no new Lean declarations — `nullity_identity` already exists; no change to the four frame axioms or to Nullity's derived status; no edit to the paper itself.

active_projects.title: lake-build-guard replays stale result for env lean FILE
active_projects.description:
Stop `lake-build-guard.sh` from replaying a stale shared result when the verified unit is a single file passed through to `env lean`.

OBSERVED LIVE, NOT HYPOTHESIZED. `bash .claude/scripts/lake-build-guard.sh build -- env lean FILE` REPLAYED the previous invocation's captured output -- errors citing line numbers of the OLD contents of FILE -- after FILE had been rewritten at the same path. The run was worked around with `--no-share`. The staleness fingerprint evidently does not cover an arbitrary file argument forwarded to `env lean`.

WHY THIS IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE ITEM IN ITS BATCH. A guard that silently replays a stale result undermines EVERY single-file verification in the system, including verifications later cited as evidence in reports, summaries and gate decisions. A stale green replay is indistinguishable from a fresh green run to the caller unless the caller inspects stderr for the `lake-build-guard: REPLAY:` marker -- the script's own usage text says exactly this under `--no-share`. The failure mode is silent acceptance of an obsolete result, not a crash, so nothing downstream flags it.

WHERE TO LOOK -- RE-DERIVE RATHER THAN TRUST; the following is a snapshot of a ~1242-line script. `collect_fingerprint_files()` documents itself as listing every `*.lean` source under the project tree. `compute_fingerprint()` defaults to `stat` mode (file METADATA), with content hashing available only opt-in via `LAKE_BUILD_GUARD_FINGERPRINT=hash`; the header notes hash mode exists specifically to close a gap stat mode leaves open. `compute_scope_key()` keys sharing on scope, and `decide_sharing()` gates the replay. The header's own list of known limitations ALREADY concedes that a caller "cannot distinguish a replay from a fresh run without passing --no-share". `LAKE_SUBCOMMANDS` includes `env` and `lean`, so an `env lean FILE` invocation passes the subcommand allowlist unremarked.

DISCRIMINATE BETWEEN TWO CANDIDATE MECHANISMS BEFORE FIXING ANYTHING -- they have different remedies and only measurement settles which occurred. (i) The rewritten FILE is not a member of the fingerprinted set at all -- it lies outside the collected root, or outside the `*.lean` glob -- so rewriting it CANNOT move the fingerprint, and no amount of strengthening the hash helps. (ii) FILE is in the set, but stat-mode metadata did not change discernibly between the two runs, in which case content hashing for named file arguments is sufficient. Reproduce the replay mechanically first; do not infer the mechanism from the header's prose.

DECIDE AND LAND ONE OF TWO. The originating request names both and they are NOT equivalent. (a) Extend the fingerprint and/or the scope key to cover the explicit file arguments of the forwarded command, so an `env lean FILE` invocation's shareability tracks FILE's own content. (b) Refuse to share a result for an `env lean ...` invocation at all -- treat it as implicitly `--no-share`. Option (b) is strictly safer and much cheaper to reason about, at the cost of giving up sharing for a real use case. Option (a) preserves sharing but must be shown correct for a file lying OUTSIDE the fingerprinted tree, which is the harder case and the one mechanism (i) above describes. If (a) is chosen, prefer content hashing over stat metadata for explicitly named file arguments regardless of the ambient `LAKE_BUILD_GUARD_FINGERPRINT` mode: stat-mode equality is the weaker predicate and this is precisely where it failed.

ACCEPTANCE -- A FAILING-FIRST REGRESSION TEST IN `tests/test-lake-build-guard.sh`, WHICH ALREADY EXISTS AND MUST BE EXTENDED RATHER THAN REPLACED. The test must: (1) run `build -- env lean FILE`; (2) rewrite FILE at the SAME path so its compile outcome changes; (3) re-run the identical command WITHOUT `--no-share`; (4) assert the second run reports the NEW outcome. Demonstrate the test fails against the unmodified script before landing the fix. Additionally, the script's documented STALENESS POLICY -- the numbered conditions in its header, which include "the record's POST-build fingerprint equals the WAITER's CURRENT fingerprint" and "a missing or empty recorded scope_key is treated as NOT shareable (fail closed)" -- MUST end up agreeing in writing with whatever behavior is landed. The acceptance condition for the documentation half is that a reader of the header alone can predict the file-argument case.

SOURCE-STORE BOUNDARY. `.claude/**` is a gitignored, regenerated deploy artifact; a hand edit there is wiped by the next deploy and will appear to succeed while having no lasting effect. Resolve `source_dir` from `<project-root>/.claude-extensions.json` for the owning extension (`core`, whose source store is `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core`) and edit at the mirroring path there, per `.claude/rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md`. Then redeploy via `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` and confirm `RESULT=landed_verify_clean`. The `.claude/**` paths in file_scope are declared only so the admission overlap gate can see the collision surface; they are NOT the edit target.

DELIVERABLE HYGIENE. Every edited file is outside `specs/**`, so its prose must carry no task-number references (`.claude/rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md`) and no record-versioning language (`.claude/rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md`). Cite durable anchors -- file names, function names, section headings, flag names -- only.

PROVENANCE. Raised during orchestration of the ladder-model cell-stabilization work and approved at the lead level as an agent-system change request. The originating issue-log entry is in `specs/760_ladder_model_cell_stabilization_lemma/issues.jsonl`, entry_id `iss_1791710205724_8rTs68` (the change request also referenced it as `iss_1791711671927_8rTs68`), severity minor, class "tooling bug or gap", resolution worked_around, hinted channel `agent_system` (hint not overridden).

active_projects.title: lean-challenge-snapshot swallows declarations, mishandles Unicode names, and over-reads Goals prose
active_projects.description:
Fix three independent defects in `lean-challenge-snapshot.sh`. The first two cause declarations to be silently lost or mangled during snapshot assembly; the third rejects plan prose that the plan-format examples permit. Defect (c) is PARTLY LANDED ALREADY as uncommitted work in the source store -- read the "ALREADY-LANDED, UNCOMMITTED SOURCE-STORE WORK" section below BEFORE touching the file, or that work will be duplicated or clobbered.

DEFECT (a) -- DECLARATION-CHUNK BOUNDARY OVER-REACH SWALLOWS `abbrev` AND ANONYMOUS `instance`. The script forces each theorem's chunk body to `:= sorry` running up to the NEXT MATCHED declaration, where the match is the alternation `(theorem|lemma|def|instance)` followed by a REQUIRED identifier. An `abbrev`, or an anonymous `instance`, sitting between two theorems therefore matches nothing and is silently absorbed into the preceding declaration's sorry body. The script's own comment concedes the mechanism in as many words: it forces the "body to `sorry` regardless of what the block actually contains." The alternation appears at more than one site (near the goal-name extractor, the body-forcing assembler, and the git-pinned signature reader) -- enumerate every occurrence rather than patching the first one found, since a fix applied to only one site leaves the others disagreeing about what counts as a declaration.

DEFECT (b) -- ASCII-ONLY IDENTIFIER REGEX, AT FOUR SITES, NOT THREE. The identifier pattern `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-zA-Z0-9_']*` appears at the three Python sites that carry the declaration alternation named in defect (a). Lean identifiers routinely contain non-ASCII characters, and such a name either escapes the Goals cross-check entirely or is TRUNCATED at its first non-ASCII character -- which is worse than escaping, because a truncated name can collide with a different real declaration. A FOURTH, non-Python site carries the same ASCII-only restriction and must be fixed with the others: the Goals extractor's `grep -oP` class, written in the equivalent lowercase-first form `[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_']*`. As of the current source-store copy the four sites are at lines 235, 446 and 564 (Python) and 382 (shell `grep -oP`); the deployed copy's line numbers differ because it is stale, and in both copies these numbers are a starting point for enumeration rather than durable anchors -- re-derive them before editing. FIXING ONLY THE PYTHON THREE IS AN INCORRECT FIX, not merely an incomplete one: it would leave the Goals identifier set and the declared identifier set disagreeing about non-ASCII names in a NEW way, and `cross_validate_identifiers()` would then report a spurious mismatch on a name both sides can see but only one side can spell. That coupling, plus the fact that defect (c)'s remaining work edits the very same `grep -oP` line, is why these defects are one record. Note in passing that the Python character class as written contains a redundant range (`A-Za-zA-Z0-9`); that is harmless today but is a sign the pattern has not been audited, and all four copies should be replaced by one shared definition rather than four independently edited literals.

DEFECT (c) -- THE GOALS BACKTICK HARVEST OVER-READS ORDINARY PROSE. The Goals-extraction pipeline, `extract_goal_names()`, treats a backtick-delimited single-word token appearing anywhere in the Goals range as a committed declaration identifier, and the harvested set is then cross-validated for EQUALITY against the Challenge declarations. A backticked namespace name, or an ordinary backticked prose word, is therefore read as a declaration name and fails cross-validation. Two of the three originally reported symptoms are already repaired (see the uncommitted-work section below); what remains unrepaired, and what this record covers, is the non-keyword case.

MEASURED RESIDUAL, AGAINST THE CURRENT SOURCE-STORE PIPELINE. For a Goals bullet reading "Prove `comm` in the `Nu` namespace, establishing a `witness` for the `EUFix` operator when the flag is `true`", the pipeline harvests `EUFix`, `Nu`, `comm`, `true`, `witness` -- four spurious identifiers for one real one. Each spurious name then appears in the "named in **Goals**: but not declared" arm of the mismatch error, and the run exits 71 on a plan that is correct as written.

WHY THE EXISTING KEYWORD DENYLIST CANNOT BE EXTENDED INTO THE FIX -- DO NOT TRY. The landed repair subtracts a closed list of Lean reserved keywords, and its safety argument is explicit and sound: Lean's lexer forbids a reserved keyword from ever being a legal declaration name, so that subtraction can never remove a real identifier. THAT ARGUMENT DOES NOT EXTEND to `Nu`, `witness`, `EUFix` or `true` -- every one of them is a legal Lean declaration name. Adding them, or any other non-keyword token, to the denylist would make the subtraction capable of removing a REAL committed identifier, converting a loud, correct mismatch into exactly the silent omission that defects (a) and (b) are about. The denylist is at its natural ceiling; the remaining fix must be structural.

A DISCRIMINATION RULE MUST BE CHOSEN DELIBERATELY, AND ONE TEMPTING OPTION IS A TRAP. Candidates to evaluate: (i) restrict extraction to a delimited identifier-bearing position inside the Goals block -- for instance a designated sub-bullet or an explicit list -- so surrounding explanatory prose is ignored by construction rather than by subtraction; (ii) introduce an explicit marker distinguishing a committed identifier from incidental backticked prose, and state it wherever the plan-format examples describe the Goals block; (iii) require a harvested token to resolve against the R1/R2-declared set before counting it as a Goal. OPTION (iii) IS THE TRAP: `cross_validate_identifiers()` compares the two sets for EQUALITY, so filtering the Goals set through the declared set makes one side a subset of the other by construction and the equality check degenerates into a tautology that can never fail. Do not adopt (iii) without first stating what the cross-check still tests afterwards; if the answer is "nothing", it is not a fix. Whichever rule is chosen, it must NARROW extraction without ever dropping a genuine Goal, and whichever rule is chosen, the accepted Goals surface must be stated in the plan-format examples too -- a script that silently accepts a narrower surface than the examples advertise is the defect this record is about, one level up.

ALREADY-LANDED, UNCOMMITTED SOURCE-STORE WORK -- READ BEFORE EDITING. The source store carries UNCOMMITTED modifications to `scripts/lean-challenge-snapshot.sh` and `scripts/tests/test-lean-challenge-snapshot.sh`, plus two UNTRACKED fixtures, `fixtures/challenge/plan_list_item_goals.md` and `fixtures/challenge/plan_keyword_noise.md`. They repair two of defect (c)'s three reported symptoms: (1) the Goals range anchors now accept the `- **Goals**:` list-item form at BOTH ends of the range (`/^-? ?\*\*Goals\*\*:/,/^-? ?\*\*[^G]/`), where previously a column-0-only anchor silently extracted NOTHING from a list-item-form plan -- and both forms are in active use among landed lean4 plans, verified in `specs/750_w_run_layer_closure_wide_lift/plans/01_w-run-layer-ladder-scheme.md` and `specs/410_internalize_tableau_branches_and_prove_routine_rule_admissibility/plans/01_internalize-routine-admissibility.md`; and (2) the reserved-keyword denylist described above. Test cases R6 (list-item form) and R7 (backticked Lean keywords in Goals prose) cover them, and the full suite reports 16 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
