The DEPLOYED `.claude/scripts/lean-challenge-snapshot.sh` does NOT yet carry any of it and still shows the old column-0 anchor, so an implementer who reads the deploy tree to establish current behavior will reach a wrong conclusion -- read the source store.

OBSERVED WORKAROUNDS, WHICH ARE THE EVIDENCE THAT THE DEFECTS BITE IN PRACTICE. For defects (a) and (b), in their originating run: every supporting definition was hoisted ahead of the first theorem and rewritten as an `abbrev`; four supporting facts were made sorry-bodied `abbrev`s rather than Goals; and the refutation probe renamed its Unicode identifiers to ASCII. For defect (c), in a later run: all non-identifier prose inside the Goals range was de-backticked and bare undotted identifiers were used, after which the tool exits 0. None of these were desired for their own sake -- each exists solely to route around one of the three defects above, which means the script is currently shaping both the Lean source and the Markdown prose that callers are allowed to write.

SUGGESTED REMEDIES TO EVALUATE (from the originating requests; evaluate, do not assume). (1) A `--dry-run` mode that also COMPILES the assembled module. Note `--dry-run` ALREADY EXISTS -- its documented behavior is to print the assembled module and the resolved `theorem_names` to stdout -- so the ask is to EXTEND it with a compile step, not to add the flag. This is the higher-leverage of the two remedies because it converts silent swallowing into a loud compile error, catching defect (a) and any future variant of it without the assembler having to enumerate every declaration keyword Lean will ever have. active_projects.title: plan-format: blocked decision gates and plan-level Status ownership
active_projects.description:
Add two missing provisions to `plan-format.md`: one admitting a pre-decided `[BLOCKED]` decision-gate phase, and one forbidding a plan from instructing the implementer to write the plan-level `Status` field.

BOTH CONCERNS ARE BATCHED INTO ONE RECORD DELIBERATELY. Each is a short prose provision in the same file, `context/formats/plan-format.md`. Splitting them would create an unordered overlap on one file's prose, which the batching guardrail in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` names as a reason to batch rather than separate. They are otherwise independent and can be landed in either order.

PROVISION 1 -- A `[BLOCKED]` DECISION GATE HAS NO LEGAL PLACE IN THE WAVE GRAPH. `plan-format.md`'s final-phase rule states that a plan's final phase MUST depend, directly or transitively, on every other phase in the plan. A phase that is already `[BLOCKED]` at PLAN time has no consistent position under that rule: making executable phases depend on it DEADLOCKS the implementer, while not depending on it violates the rule's letter. The file's "Decision gates and contingency branches" subsection introduces decision gates but says nothing about one that is blocked before execution begins. Resolved ad hoc in the originating run by placing the blocked gate in wave 1 beside the first executable phase with `Depends on: none`, and noting in the wave table that the final phase re-observes the gate's measurement through the wired probe. PRECEDENT EXISTS AND SHOULD BE READ BEFORE DRAFTING: `specs/archive/006` plan 05 and `specs/archive/008` plan 03 (locate the exact paths by globbing the archive -- the directory names carry slugs). A one-paragraph provision in the "Decision gates and contingency branches" subsection settles it. The provision must say explicitly how such a gate relates to the final-phase transitive-dependency rule, so that a plan validator and a human reader reach the same verdict on a plan containing one; a provision that merely permits the shape without reconciling it against the final-phase rule leaves the ambiguity in place.

PROVISION 2 -- PLANNER-SIDE GUIDANCE PERMITS AUTHORING AN INSTRUCTION THE IMPLEMENTER IS FORBIDDEN TO EXECUTE. In the originating run a plan's final phase instructed the implementer to set the plan-level `- **Status**:` field to `[BLOCKED]`. The `lean-implementation-agent` contract (its MUST-NOT item citing `context/contracts/plan-status-ownership.md`) reserves that field for `update-plan-status.sh` via `update-task-status.sh` postflight. The agent CORRECTLY followed the contract and annotated the checklist item as a skipped deviation -- so nothing malfunctioned at run time; the defect is that the instruction was writable at all. THE FIX BELONGS ON THE PLANNER/PLAN-FORMAT SIDE so such an instruction is never authored. Concretely: `plan-format.md` already documents the plan-level `- **Status**:` field, its required-field list, and its trailing-annotation rule under "Plan-level vs. phase-level markers" -- add, at that same place, an explicit statement that the field is owned by `update-plan-status.sh` and that NO phase checklist item may instruct a writer to set it, together with what a planner should write instead when it wants a plan to end up `[BLOCKED]`. That last clause is load-bearing: a prohibition with no sanctioned alternative will be worked around. Evaluate whether `agents/planner-agent.md` needs a matching line, since that file carries the plan template and the required-field checks the planner actually executes; if `plan-format.md` alone is judged sufficient, say so in the plan and drop the planner-agent path from the edit set rather than leaving it ambiguous.

ACCEPTANCE. (1) A reader of `plan-format.md` alone can determine whether a plan containing a pre-decided `[BLOCKED]` gate conforms, and can predict where that gate sits in the wave table. (2) A reader of `plan-format.md` alone can determine that the plan-level `Status` field is not writable from a phase checklist item, and can find the sanctioned alternative. (4) No change to the closed six-value phase-marker enum or to the `### Phase N: {name} [STATUS]` heading contract, both of which have mechanical consumers (`update-phase-status.sh`, `update-plan-status.sh`, `update-task-status.sh --phase-check`) that this record must not disturb.

active_projects.title: postflight writes detail-free blocking issue entry on partial returns
active_projects.description:
Stop the orchestrate postflight from writing a detail-free blocking issue-log entry on every blocker-bearing partial return, and settle that entry's classification.

ROOT CAUSE IS A TYPE MISMATCH, MEASURED NOT HYPOTHESIZED -- THE DETAIL WAS AVAILABLE AND WAS THROWN AWAY. In `scripts/orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh`, the `partial)` arm of the dispatch-status case statement builds the issue narrative with `partial_blockers_detail=$(echo "${handoff:-null}" | jq -r '(.blockers // []) | join("; ")' 2>/dev/null)`, then substitutes a literal fallback string when that comes back empty. The handoff's `blockers[]` is an array of OBJECTS, not strings: `scripts/validate-handoff.sh` requires each entry to carry `phase` and `target` (it counts an entry lacking them as an invalid blocker), and the live returns carry `{phase, target, verbatim_goal, what_was_tried, why_it_failed}`. `jq`'s `join` on an array of objects does not degrade -- it ERRORS (`string ("") and object ... cannot be added`, exit 5). The `2>/dev/null` swallows the error, the command substitution yields the empty string, the `-z` guard fires, and the literal fallback text is what gets recorded. Re-derive this before fixing: run the `join("; ")` expression against a blocker-bearing `.return-meta.json` WITHOUT `2>/dev/null` and read the jq error directly. Note the arm is only reachable when the blocker count is already greater than zero, so the fallback branch as written is reachable ONLY through this error path -- a non-empty array that joins to an empty string is otherwise impossible. That makes the fallback string a permanent output, not a rare degradation.

WHAT THE LOST DETAIL ACTUALLY WAS, AND WHY THE LOSS MATTERS MORE THAN THE NOISE. The discarded `blockers[]` objects carried the refuted goal statement verbatim, what had been tried, and why it failed -- several paragraphs of exactly the content the log exists to preserve. `context/formats/issue-log.md`'s surface-relation table states the MIRROR obligation this call site is implementing: the handoff keeps naming blockers for the immediate successor dispatch, but because `.orchestrator-handoff.json` is overwritten on every dispatch, a `blockers[]` entry about to be written should ALSO be recorded via `issue-record.sh` so the detail survives the overwrite. The call site's own in-code comment cites that obligation by name. The obligation is therefore currently discharged in form and defeated in substance: the entry exists, the detail it was supposed to rescue is gone, and the handoff that held it has since been overwritten. This half of the record is the high-value half and is wholly independent of the classification question below -- land it first.

THE TEST SUITE PASSES OVER THE DEFECT. `scripts/tests/test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh` already has a regression case for a blocker-bearing partial, and it already uses object-shaped blockers (`target`, `verbatim_goal`, `why_it_failed`). It asserts only the state.json status transition and the aux signal -- never the recorded `what_happened` text -- so the suite is green while the narrative is empty. ACCEPTANCE for the detail half: extend that existing case (do not replace it) to assert that the recorded `issues.jsonl` entry's `what_happened` contains content drawn from the blocker objects, and show the assertion fails against the unmodified script. Decide explicitly how an object is rendered into one prose paragraph -- which subfields are included, in what order, and what happens when an optional subfield is absent -- rather than leaving the format implicit in a jq expression. Removing the `2>/dev/null` on this particular substitution, or otherwise surfacing a jq failure here instead of silently substituting, is in scope: a swallowed error is what converted a fixable bug into an invisible one.

CLASSIFICATION: THREE SEPARABLE QUESTIONS, ONLY ONE OF WHICH THE ORIGINATING REQUEST SETTLED. (1) CLASS. The call site hard-codes `--class "environment"`, whose admission test in `issue-log.md`'s seed-class table is "the local or CI environment (missing binary, version mismatch, permissions) caused the cost". A blocker-bearing partial is almost never that -- in the originating run the blocker was a refuted mathematical statement. The class is wrong for the general case, and it is hard-coded where the actual class is not knowable from the postflight's vantage point; evaluate whether a less specific but honest class, or a class derived from the handoff, is the right remedy. (2) SEVERITY. The call site hard-codes `--severity blocking`. Unlike the class, this appears DEFENSIBLE against the four-rung scale in `issue-log.md`'s "Severity Scale": `blocking` is admitted when "work could not proceed at all ... the dispatch stalled or had to hand off because of it", which is precisely a blocker-bearing partial. Do not reclassify severity merely to reduce channel volume -- if the entry is genuinely blocking, suppressing it by downgrading severity hides a real signal. Argue the severity question on the admission test, and record the argument. (3) VOLUME. The same unresolved blocker is re-recorded on every subsequent partial dispatch: the originating task carries two entries with byte-identical `what_happened`, differing only in `entry_id`, `timestamp`, `dispatch_seq` and `session_id`. Even with full detail restored, N dispatches against one unresolved blocker yield N near-duplicate blocking entries. Consider de-duplication keyed on blocker identity rather than on dispatch.

THE SUPPRESSION IDEA HAS AN ORDERING OBSTACLE -- CHECK IT BEFORE COSTING IT. The originating request asks to consider suppressing the entry entirely when the partial outcome already carries a `user_decision` payload that was relayed and answered. In the current script the `user_decision` relay is a LATER work block (its own section, several hundred lines below the `partial)` arm), so at the moment the issue is written the relay has not yet run. Suppression therefore requires reading `user_decision` off the handoff early, or deferring the issue write until after the relay -- not a one-line guard. Also decide what "answered" means mechanically: `return-metadata-file.md` documents `user_decision` as producer-owned and relayed-never-resolved, so the presence of the payload does not by itself establish that the user answered. If no mechanical test for "answered" exists, say so and scope the suppression to the weaker, checkable condition or drop it with that reason recorded.

DO NOT ENCROACH ON THE CONCLUSION-STAGE FILTER PREDICATE. Whether a reclassified entry still reaches a channel is governed by `context/contracts/conclusion-stage.md`'s "The Filter Predicate" (an entry enters classification only when `resolution` is `open` or `worked_around`). A separate record -- the one covering null-resolution entries being dropped by the conclusion stage -- owns that predicate, `scripts/issue-record.sh`, and `context/formats/issue-log.md`. This record MUST confine its edits to this call site's own arguments and the postflight script plus its test, leaving the predicate, the writer script, and the format document to that record. If that record has already landed a predicate change by the time this one is implemented, read the predicate as it then stands and honor it. If a prose amendment to `issue-log.md` is judged genuinely necessary, add a serializing dependency edge at that point (`update-task-status.sh --depends-on-add`) rather than editing a file another record claims -- the file_scope declared here is deliberately disjoint from it for exactly this reason.

SOURCE-STORE BOUNDARY. `.claude/**` is a gitignored, regenerated deploy artifact; a hand edit there is wiped by the next deploy and will appear to succeed while having no lasting effect. Resolve `source_dir` from `<project-root>/.claude-extensions.json` for the owning extension (`core`, whose source store is `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core`) and edit at the mirroring path there, per `.claude/rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md`. Then redeploy via `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` and confirm `RESULT=landed_verify_clean`. The `.claude/**` path in file_scope is declared only so the admission overlap gate can see the collision surface; it is NOT the edit target.

DELIVERABLE HYGIENE. Every edited file is outside `specs/**`, so its prose must carry no task-number references (`.claude/rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md`) and no record-versioning language (`.claude/rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md`). Cite durable anchors -- file names, function names, section headings, field names, flag names -- only.

PROVENANCE. Raised during orchestration of the ladder-model cell-stabilization work and approved at the lead level as an agent-system change request. The originating issue-log entries are in `specs/760_ladder_model_cell_stabilization_lemma/issues.jsonl`, entry_ids `iss_1791711671927_JbPqvi` (dispatch_seq 3) and `iss_1791716590257_0MGDRu` (dispatch_seq 6); both severity `blocking`, class `environment`, resolution `open`. CHANNEL OVERRIDE, RECORDED VISIBLY: both entries' own `suggested_channel` hint reads `follow_up_task`; the orchestrate lead OVERRODE the hint to `agent_system`, on the ground that the defect lies in the orchestrator's own issue-writing path rather than in any task's subject-matter work -- there is no task to follow up, only a writer to fix. `conclusion-stage.md`'s "The Hint-Versus-Decision Rule" sanctions that override provided it is stated visibly, which this paragraph is.

RELATED RECORDS, FOR ORIENTATION ONLY -- NO DEPENDENCY EDGES. Three sibling records from the same orchestration cover the `lake-build-guard.sh` stale-replay defect, the `lean-challenge-snapshot.sh` declaration-chunk and Unicode-identifier defects, and the `plan-format.md` blocked-decision-gate and plan-level-Status-ownership provisions; all three touch files disjoint from this one. The null-resolution conclusion-stage record is the nearest neighbour and is the one whose territory this record must not enter, as stated above.

active_projects.title: planned jq rewrites re-serialize formatting-sensitive JSON record files
active_projects.description:
Add agent-system guidance for in-place edits of formatting-sensitive JSON record files, so a whole-file `jq` rewrite is never authored as the edit mechanism for one.

MEASURED, NOT HYPOTHESIZED. A plan step phrased "with jq, set T4/T6 description ..." was executed against `specs/757_lplus_decidability_successor_task_set/successor-records.json`. Piping that file through `jq` re-serialized it: every compact one-line dependency object -- T1/T2/T3/T5, records the step never intended to touch -- was re-flowed into multi-line form, yielding 44 changed lines for 5 intended field changes. `jq` has no formatting-preserving mode; it parses to a value and prints that value in its own style, so a whole-file pipe through it rewrites the ENTIRE file's layout whether or not the filter touches a given record.

NOTHING IN THE REPOSITORY IS BROKEN. The affected file was repaired in the originating run and is correct as it stands; do not re-edit it, and do not treat this record as a data-repair record. This record's entire deliverable is prose in the source store.

THE ALTERNATIVE MECHANISM IS ALREADY PROVEN AND MUST BE WRITTEN DOWN CONCRETELY, NOT GESTURED AT. The originating run's workaround was: take the HEAD version of the file as the starting bytes; apply the intended field changes as a TEXT-level edit (in that run: two description literals, two `why` values, one appended `_amended` key); separately compute the intended result with `jq`; assert the two agree as JSON under canonicalization -- e.g. `diff <(jq -S . text-edited) <(jq -S . jq-output)` must be empty -- and only then move the text-level edit into place. THE ASSERTION IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF: it buys back the one thing a text-level edit gives up, namely jq's guarantee that the result is well-formed JSON carrying the intended values. Guidance that says "edit it by hand instead" WITHOUT the equality assertion is worse than no guidance, because a hand edit of JSON silently admits a trailing comma or a broken escape. Write the recipe out as runnable lines a reader can copy, including where the HEAD bytes come from (`git show HEAD:<path>`) and the move-into-place step.

BOTH AUDIENCES MUST BE REACHED, AND THEY READ DIFFERENT FILES. (i) A PLAN AUTHOR must not author "with jq, set X" as a step against such a file in the first place -- the defect originated in a plan step, not in an implementer's improvisation. (ii) An IMPLEMENTER handed such a step must find the alternative without first having to discover the term "re-serialization". A siting that reaches only one of the two leaves half the defect in place; state in the plan which path reaches which audience.

SITING -- DECIDE EXPLICITLY, DO NOT LEAVE IT AMBIGUOUS. Two candidates; the deciding criterion is UNPROMPTED discoverability, i.e. an agent that has just been handed a jq edit step and does not yet know this failure class exists must still land on the guidance. (a) A new section in `context/patterns/jq-escaping-workarounds.md`. That file's title names a DIFFERENT failure class (Claude Code Issue #1132's `!=` escaping), but it is the de facto jq-pitfalls hub: roughly eighteen files across core already point at it, and the deployed `CLAUDE.md`'s "jq Command Safety" section -- sourced from `merge-sources/claudemd.md` -- names it as the full documentation. Discovery is therefore free, at the cost of a file whose title under-describes its contents; if (a) is chosen, widen that file's own framing so a reader is not surprised to meet a second, unrelated failure class inside it. (b) A new sibling pattern file, conceptually cleaner but starting with zero referrers; if (b) is chosen, the referrer wiring and the `index-entries.json` entry are part of THIS change rather than a follow-up, because an unreferenced pattern file is not guidance, it is a file. Either way, add one line to `merge-sources/claudemd.md`'s existing "jq Command Safety" section: that merged section is the surface every session already reads and is the cheapest path to the plan-author audience.

IF SITING (b) IS CHOSEN, WIDEN file_scope BEFORE CREATING THE FILE. The new path must be added through `update-task-status.sh` rather than written into a file_scope-unlisted location silently.

SCOPE DECISION, ALREADY MADE AT FILING TIME: GUIDANCE ONLY, NO HELPER SCRIPT. The originating request asked whether a small formatting-preserving helper script belongs alongside the prose. It does not, and the reasons are recorded here so the question is not re-litigated during research. (1) The proven mechanism is three lines of shell, and the part that is actual WORK -- authoring the text-level edit for this particular file and these particular fields -- cannot be factored into a script; a wrapper would automate only the assertion. (2) A genuinely general formatting-preserving JSON editor (surgical field replacement that preserves per-record compaction and key order) is a substantial program needing its own test suite, deploy registration and ongoing maintenance, out of all proportion to one minor, already-worked-around entry. (3) The nearest existing wrapper, `scripts/state-write.sh`, exists for a reason that does NOT transfer: it serializes many automated, concurrent call sites against one hot file (`specs/state.json`) behind a fail-closed mutex. Record files are edited by a single implementer inside a planned step; a wrapper buys no concurrency safety there and adds an interface to learn. THE REOPEN CONDITION, which the guidance itself should name: if some record file turns out to be edited often enough that the assertion recipe is being retyped repeatedly, revisit the script question then.

WHAT THE GUIDANCE MUST NOT SAY. Do not generalize this into "jq is unsafe for JSON edits". jq remains the correct tool for `specs/state.json` (through `state-write.sh`), for computing the intended value in the recipe above, and for every file whose byte-level layout nobody depends on. State the trigger condition in terms a reader can CHECK before acting: the file is committed with a layout a round-trip through `jq` would not reproduce (hand-maintained compaction, a deliberate key order, mixed compact-and-expanded records), AND the edit is meant to touch a few fields rather than rewrite the file. Name `specs/state.json`'s wrapper as the adjacent-but-different case and say plainly that record files have no such wrapper -- which is exactly why this discipline has to live in prose rather than in a script.

ACCEPTANCE. (1) A reader arriving from the deployed `CLAUDE.md` jq section, or from any existing referrer of the jq pattern file, reaches the new guidance without knowing the term "re-serialization" in advance. (2) The guidance carries a copyable recipe INCLUDING the canonicalized JSON-equality assertion, not merely a prohibition. (3) The guidance states a checkable trigger condition and names at least one concrete file shape that meets it. (4) The guidance states the `state-write.sh` relation and does not imply a wrapper exists for record files. (5) If a new file is created it carries an `index-entries.json` entry and at least one referrer; if an existing file is extended, that file's `index-entries.json` entry (`line_count`, `keywords`) is brought back into agreement with the file. (6) `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` reports `RESULT=landed_verify_clean` afterwards.

Resolve `source_dir` from `<project-root>/.claude-extensions.json` for the owning extension (`core`, whose source store is `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core`) and edit at the mirroring path there, per `.claude/rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md`. Then redeploy via `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` and confirm `RESULT=landed_verify_clean`. The `.claude/**` path in file_scope is declared only so the admission overlap gate can see the collision surface; it is NOT the edit target.

Every edited file lies outside `specs/**`, so its prose must carry no task-number references (`.claude/rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md`) and no record-versioning language (`.claude/rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md`). The originating file path, the tool name and the field names are durable anchors and may be cited; the originating task number and the issue entry_id may NOT appear in the guidance prose -- they live in this record only.

PROVENANCE. Raised during orchestration of the ladder-frame carrier repair work and approved at the lead level as an agent-system change request. The originating issue-log entry is in `specs/765_ladder_frame_carrier_repair_and_index_deletion/issues.jsonl`, entry_id `iss_1791760497369_ipMdVR` -- class `tool_side_effect`, severity `minor`, phase `implement`, dispatch_seq 2, resolution `worked_around`. The entry carried NO `suggested_channel` hint, so there is no hint-versus-decision override to state: the orchestrate lead classified it to the agent-system channel on its own judgment, on the ground that the remedy is agent-system guidance rather than repository work product.

RELATED RECORDS, FOR ORIENTATION ONLY -- NO DEPENDENCY EDGES AS FILED. `agent-system/extensions/core/agents/planner-agent.md` is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from this record's file_scope even though the plan-author audience makes it a tempting edit target: the plan-format blocked-decision-gate record already claims that path. If research concludes a matching line in `planner-agent.md` is genuinely necessary, add a serializing dependency edge at that point (`update-task-status.sh --depends-on-add`) rather than editing a file another record claims. No other active agent-system record touches the jq pattern file, `index-entries.json`, or `merge-sources/claudemd.md`; re-check that at admission time, since any concurrently filed record that adds a new context file will also touch `index-entries.json`.

**EVALUATE (AND BE WILLING TO DECLINE): should plan guidance require a refuted predicted REASON to be recorded distinctly from a refuted predicted OUTCOME?**

**THIS IS A DELIBERATELY WEAK PROPOSAL. "No change needed" is a genuinely available and fully acceptable conclusion, not a formality.** The originating finding is already completely recorded in-tree, no in-tree work remains, and the convention that captured it appears to have worked as designed. Read the "WHY THIS EXISTS AT ALL" section below before deciding how much effort to spend; a short report concluding "the current convention suffices, here is why" is a successful outcome of this record.

**CITATION (the sole evidence this record is built from).** Task 773, issue-log entry `entry_id: iss_1791780659461_iJw5zy` in `specs/773_ladder_cell_index_factorization/issues.jsonl` — `class: plan-accuracy`, `severity: minor`, `phase: implement`, `dispatch_seq: 3`, `resolution: null` (implicit-open), `evidence_path: null`, `suggested_channel: null`. Read that entry verbatim before composing anything. Because the entry carried no `suggested_channel`, the conclusion stage's channel assignment overrode no hint.

**WHAT WAS OBSERVED.** Task 773's plan was written falsify-first: each of Phase 2's enumerated attempts had its expected outcome written down before it ran, with both branches pre-specified. Attempt (iii-a) then confirmed the plan's predicted OUTCOME (no refutation) but REFUTED its predicted REASON. The plan expected an achievable-window argument positioned by the residue coordinates; the measured mechanism was stronger and simpler — `Count false false` holds the countdown at `0` through an idle interval of any length while `Drift` moves the next deadline freely, so every second-region length is reachable from every pending state (`second_region_any_length`), and the achievable second-region-end tag set is everything, independently of `T`, `P` and `B`. No plan step was skipped or substituted, and the correct reason was recorded in the landed probe and in the task's summary.

**THE QUESTION TO PUT.** Today a plan's both-outcomes wording covers the OUTCOME axis. The reason axis was recorded here only because the implementing dispatch chose, on its own initiative, to log it as an issue — nothing required it. Should falsify-first plan guidance require that a refuted predicted reason be recorded distinctly from a refuted outcome?

**GROUNDING ALREADY DONE — DO NOT REDO IT, BUT DO RE-VERIFY IT.** A source-store search was performed when this record was filed. Four findings, each of which weakens or redirects the premise:

1. **There is no system-level falsify-first plan convention to tighten.** `context/formats/plan-format.md`'s per-phase required field list is Goal, Tasks, Timing, Depends on, Verification Tier, Commit Mode — it contains NO predicted-outcome field of any kind. The pre-written expected outcomes with both branches pre-specified were a property of task 773's OWN plan style, authored by that task, not an instance of a documented standard. Consequently the change contemplated here would mean INTRODUCING a plan-authoring convention, not refining an existing one. That is a materially larger and weaker-motivated proposal than "tighten the wording", and the burden of justification should rise accordingly.
2. **`context/contracts/phase-closure.md` contains no predicted-outcome or predicted-reason machinery either.** Its uses of "outcome" refer to terminal dispatch outcomes and status markers, not to plan predictions. It is probably not the right home for such a requirement.
3. **A refutation-recording mechanism already exists and must be checked before anything new is proposed.** `context/formats/return-metadata-file.md` defines an invalidated-claims structure with `kind: "refutation" | "supersession"`, `claim`, `evidence_path`, and `declaration_names`, consumed by `scripts/sweep-invalidated-claims.sh`. A refuted predicted reason is plausibly already expressible there. Determine whether it is, and whether task 773's finding should simply have been filed through that channel, BEFORE designing any new field or prose requirement. Note that mechanism's own documented precision-over-recall posture (it matches declaration names literally and misses paraphrase) when judging whether it genuinely fits.
4. **The cheapest real candidate change here may be a classification question, not a plan-format change.** `context/formats/issue-log.md` defines a 15-class seed enum in its "Seed Class Enum" section; `plan-accuracy` is NOT among the 15. `class` is explicitly an open vocabulary, and that same document's "Unknown-Class Tally" section already assigns the conclusion stage the job of tallying non-seed classes across tasks and names recurrence as the criterion for promoting one into the seed enum. The observed phenomenon also sits close to the existing seed class `design-record defect or ambiguity` ("the design record was wrong... or silent on a case the implementer actually hit"). So three live options exist that require no plan-format change at all: (a) the finding maps onto `design-record defect or ambiguity` and the existing taxonomy already covers it; (b) `plan-accuracy` is a promotion candidate to be decided by recurrence, per the mechanism already documented, which means the correct action now is to WAIT for recurrence rather than legislate; (c) nothing changes.

**WHY THIS EXISTS AT ALL — stated plainly, because it bears on how much effort is warranted.** The conclusion stage's exactly-one-channel rule (`context/contracts/conclusion-stage.md`, "The Exactly-One-Channel Rule") requires every classified non-win entry to land in exactly one of its three output channels. That rule is what forced this observation into a channel rather than letting it remain informational, and the lead that dispatched it classified it as a deliberately weak proposal and said so to the user when seeking approval. One `minor`-severity, single-occurrence observation, already fully recorded in the landed probe and the task's own issue log and summary, with the existing both-outcomes convention having behaved as designed, is thin evidence for changing a shared standard. Do not manufacture a change to justify the record's existence. If the honest answer is that a single occurrence does not warrant a standards change and the right move is to wait for recurrence under the mechanism issue-log.md already documents, say exactly that and close.

**SCOPE.** (1) Read the cited entry verbatim and re-verify the four grounding findings above against the live source store rather than trusting this summary. (2) Decide among: no change; record the finding's correct existing home (the invalidated-claims mechanism and/or the `design-record defect or ambiguity` seed class) in whichever document would prevent the next implementer from facing the same ambiguity; defer pending recurrence per the Unknown-Class Tally mechanism; or, only if genuinely justified, introduce an explicit predicted-reason recording requirement and specify which document owns it. (3) Whatever is decided, write down the reasoning so the next occurrence can be judged against it instead of re-litigated from scratch.

**NON-GOALS.** No change to task 773's landed work, which is complete and correct — the probe records the right reason. No re-opening of the ladder/cell-index factorization result itself. No new issue-log class invented without applying the recurrence criterion the taxonomy already specifies. No new plan-level required field added merely to close this record.

**SOURCE-STORE BOUNDARY.** Every candidate edit target here lives in a deployed, regenerated tree: a hand edit under `.claude/**` is silently wiped by the next deploy. Resolve `source_dir` from `<project-root>/.claude-extensions.json` for the owning extension — for all documents named above this is core, at `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core` — and edit at the mirroring path (`context/formats/plan-format.md`, `context/contracts/phase-closure.md`, `context/formats/issue-log.md`), then redeploy. Per `.claude/rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md`. The deployed paths in `file_scope` are declared only so the overlap gate can see the collision surface; they are NOT the edit target.

active_projects.title: Carve a task's own specs/ artifacts out of git-commit-phase.sh's containment filter
active_projects.description:
Carve a task's own specs/ artifacts out of git-commit-phase.sh's containment filter, so a task's own plan file is never dropped from its own phase commit.

READ THIS FIRST -- THE DESIGN QUESTION IS ALREADY ANSWERED BY TWO EXISTING CONTRACT TEXTS, AND THIS IS A CODE/CONTRACT DIVERGENCE, NOT A POLICY DECISION. The originating change request asks whether a task's own `specs/{NNN}_{SLUG}/` artifacts SHOULD be implicitly in scope for its own phase commits rather than requiring explicit `file_scope` declaration. Both documents that specify this filter already say YES, unambiguously and in detail. The implementation does not do it. The work is therefore to make the code match its own already-written specification, plus to correct the one false premise in the standard that let the gap through -- NOT to deliberate the policy afresh.

MEASURED ROOT CAUSE, RE-DERIVABLE IN TWO READS. In `scripts/git-commit-phase.sh` the fixed scope is appended to `stage_paths` first and unconditionally: `stage_paths=("${task_dir}/" "specs/TODO.md" "specs/state.json")`, plus `$plan_path` when `--plan-path` is given. Separately, `files_touched` is DERIVED from `${task_dir}/progress/phase-{P}-progress.json` by unioning `.objectives[].files_touched[]`. The Phase-Commit Containment Self-Check then runs its `is_contained()` predicate over `files_touched` -- and `is_contained()` tests each path ONLY against the entries of the task's declared `file_scope` array. It does not treat `task_dir` as an implicit in-scope member, and it does not carve the four fixed paths out of the loop. The two lists OVERLAP: a path can be both unconditionally staged via `${task_dir}/` and simultaneously present in the derived `files_touched`. When an implementation agent self-reports its own plan artifact in `files_touched` -- which is ordinary, expected behaviour, because the implement phase is supposed to annotate the plan with checklist ticks and phase-heading closure -- that path reaches the filter and is dropped.

THE STANDARD'S OWN STATED REASON WHY THIS CANNOT HAPPEN IS THE FALSE PREMISE. `context/standards/git-staging-scope.md`, in its "Staging-Layer Containment Filter (a Refinement of the Fail-Safe Direction Above)" subsection, asserts: "The four `specs/` carve-out paths (`TASK_DIR/`, `TODO.md`, `state.json`, and the plan path for `implement`) are never tested against this filter at all -- they are appended to the staged set before the filtered loop runs, structurally outside its reach." The conclusion is correct as policy; the stated mechanism is wrong. Being appended to `stage_paths` confers no protection whatsoever on an entry of the SEPARATE `files_touched` list, which is what the loop actually iterates. That sentence is the reason no one noticed the predicate was missing its carve-out, and correcting it is part of this record's deliverable -- a fix that repairs the code while leaving this sentence standing would leave the next reader with the same false assurance.

THE AGENT PROSE, BY CONTRAST, IS ALREADY CORRECT -- DO NOT EDIT IT. `agents/general-implementation-agent.md`'s "Phase-Commit Containment Self-Check" step 2 states the required behaviour exactly: "Carve out of the check entirely: this task's own task directory (`specs/{NNN}_{SLUG}/`), `specs/TODO.md`, `specs/state.json`, and the plan path. These four are unconditionally staged by the wrapper and are never themselves task deliverables, so testing them for containment would produce a guaranteed false positive on every single commit." That is the specification the script was ported from and failed to implement. It needs no change; it is the authority the fix should be verified against. Treat any temptation to edit it as a signal that the fix has drifted.

THE REAL COST IS A DISABLED SAFETY GATE, NOT THE WARNING NOISE -- THIS IS MEASURED, NOT PREDICTED. In the observed occurrence the task's phase-1 progress file listed EXACTLY ONE `files_touched` entry, and it was the task's own plan artifact (verify: `jq -r '[.objectives[].files_touched[]?]|unique' specs/771_task_reference_lint_debt_boneyard_tests/progress/phase-1-progress.json` returns a single-element array naming `plans/01_verify-lint-gate-green.md`). The filter dropped that one entry, `kept_files_touched` came back empty, `files_touched` was reassigned to the empty array, and the script therefore set `run_completeness_check=false`. The post-commit completeness check -- the exit-6 detector that this script's own header describes as existing to catch "the exact silent-drop shape this script exists to catch, whatever the underlying mechanism" -- was consequently SKIPPED ENTIRELY for that phase commit. So the failure mode is self-defeating in the worst available way: a false-positive scope drop silently disarms the very gate whose job is to detect silent drops, and it does so precisely in the common case where a phase's only self-reported file is the plan the phase annotated. Any fix MUST be verified to restore `run_completeness_check` in that single-plan-file case, not merely to suppress the warning.

HONEST SEVERITY BOUND -- NO COMMITTED DATA WAS LOST, AND THE RECORD SHOULD NOT CLAIM OTHERWISE. Because `${task_dir}/` is staged unconditionally, the plan file did reach the commit: `git log --oneline --all -- specs/771_task_reference_lint_debt_boneyard_tests/plans/01_verify-lint-gate-green.md` shows it in the phase commit (`task 771 phase 1: verify lint gate green and attribute the fix`) and in the completion commit. The originating entry's `minor` severity is therefore correct for data loss. The three genuine costs are (1) the disabled completeness check above, (2) a false WARNING on stderr that trains readers to discount a warning that is load-bearing for genuine excursions, and (3) a spurious `scope excursion` entry written to `issues.jsonl` via `issue-record.sh`, which then consumed a conclusion-stage channel slot and produced this very record -- a self-inflicted feedback loop whose token cost exceeds the fix's.

WHERE THE FIX BELONGS, AND WHY THE TWO ALTERNATIVE SITES ARE WRONG. The request names three candidate sites; evaluate them in this order and record the reasoning.
  (a) `git-commit-phase.sh`'s predicate -- CORRECT SITE. Carve the four fixed paths out before the filtered loop, or equivalently admit `task_dir` plus `specs/TODO.md`, `specs/state.json` and `$plan_path` as implicit in-scope members inside `is_contained()`. Prefer whichever form makes the carve-out visibly parallel to the `stage_paths` construction a few lines above, so the two can be read together. Note that `task_dir` is derived locally in the script already (`task_dir="specs/${padded_num}_${project_name}"`), so the fix needs no new input or lookup.
  (b) `file_scope` declaration/derivation at task creation -- REJECT, with reason recorded. Adding `specs/{NNN}_{SLUG}/` to every task's declared `file_scope` would make a redundant explicit declaration mandatory forever, on every task, to restate something two contract documents already declare implicit; it would also push synthetic entries into the SEPARATE consumers of `file_scope` -- the Overlap-family contention machinery (`scripts/lib/file-scope-overlap.sh`, `scripts/lib/territory-contention-lib.sh`, `git-commit-scoped.sh`'s V5 contended-path gate) and `scripts/backfill-file-scope.sh` -- which exist to reason about SHARED source-tree territory between tasks, not about a directory only one task can ever own. Keep `file_scope` meaning "the source-tree territory this task may modify".
  (c) `context/standards/git-staging-scope.md` -- NEEDED, BUT AS A CORRECTION, NOT AS THE FIX. The policy there is already right; only the "structurally outside its reach" mechanism sentence is wrong. Replace it with an accurate statement of how the carve-out is actually achieved once (a) lands. Do not restate the policy a third time or introduce a second differently-worded convention.

THE "MAKE IT LOUD" FALLBACK IS MOOT FOR THIS CLASS, BUT MUST NOT BE TRADED AWAY FOR THE OTHER CLASS. The request asks that, if implicit inclusion is rejected, the drop be made loud at minimum. Implicit inclusion is NOT rejected -- it is already the contract -- so for a task's own artifacts the correct end state is no warning and no issue entry at all, because there is no excursion to report. Preserve the existing drop-and-warn behaviour, the `issue-record.sh` call, and the fail-open-on-missing-`file_scope` behaviour UNCHANGED for genuine out-of-scope paths; four such genuine drops are already on record in `specs/754_plan_postflight_file_scope_widening_silent/issues.jsonl` (naming real source-store paths), and those are the filter working as designed. The fix must narrow the predicate's false positives without weakening its true positives.

NO INTERACTION WITH `--allow-out-of-scope` OR THE FILE-SCOPE-WIDENING MECHANISM -- VERIFIED, AND THE NON-INTERACTION SHOULD BE STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. These are three mechanisms at three layers and the fix touches only the first: (i) this containment filter, in `git-commit-phase.sh`, deciding what is PASSED to the commit script; (ii) `--allow-out-of-scope`, which belongs to `scripts/git-snapshot.sh`'s rollback-refusal path, not to the commit path at all; (iii) additive `file_scope` widening at plan postflight, via `scripts/plan-file-scope-harvest.sh` forwarding `--file-scope-add=<json>` to `scripts/update-task-status.sh` (whose merge clause is `(.file_scope) |= ((. // []) + $add | unique)`). Confirm each of these three before writing, and do not route the fix through (ii) or (iii): widening a task's declared `file_scope` to cover its own artifacts is route (b) above under a different name, and is rejected for the same reasons.

ACCEPTANCE. (1) A regression case added to `scripts/tests/test-git-commit-phase.sh` -- extend the suite, do not replace its existing Case 7 (genuine out-of-scope drop) or Case 8 (fail-open on missing `file_scope`), both of which must stay green and are the guard against over-correction. The new case fixtures a task whose declared `file_scope` names only source paths, whose progress file's sole `files_touched` entry is its own plan artifact under `${task_dir}/`, and asserts all four of: the plan path is NOT dropped; no `dropping out-of-scope path` warning naming it is emitted; no `scope excursion` entry is written for it; and the post-commit completeness check RUNS rather than being skipped. (2) Demonstrate the new case FAILS against the unmodified script before the fix lands -- the current suite is green while the defect is live, so a case that cannot fail first proves nothing. (3) Add coverage for `specs/TODO.md` and `specs/state.json` self-reported in `files_touched` as well; they are exposed by exactly the same gap and the carve-out names them. (4) Redeploy via `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` and confirm `RESULT=landed_verify_clean`.

NON-GOALS. No change to `agents/general-implementation-agent.md` (its prose is the correct specification). No change to the drop-and-warn policy, the `issue-record.sh` integration, or the fail-open direction for genuine excursions. No change to `git-commit-scoped.sh` or any of its V-gates -- the filter is sited one layer above and the exit-code contract is untouched. No retroactive cleanup of the already-written spurious issue entry. No migration of the per-extension implementation agents' hand-typed `stage_paths` arrays to this wrapper; `git-staging-scope.md`'s "Scope of the `git-commit-phase.sh` migration" paragraph already records that as a separately-scoped follow-up and it stays that way. Empty-array expansion under `set -euo pipefail` is safe on bash 4.4 and later (this host runs 5.3), so the existing `"${files_touched[@]}"` expansions need no defensive change -- do not add one.

SOURCE-STORE BOUNDARY. `.claude/**` is a gitignored, regenerated deploy artifact; a hand edit there is silently wiped by the next deploy and will appear to succeed while having no lasting effect. The owning extension is `core`, whose `source_dir` resolves from `<project-root>/.claude-extensions.json` to `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core`. Edit at the mirroring paths there -- `scripts/git-commit-phase.sh`, `scripts/tests/test-git-commit-phase.sh`, `context/standards/git-staging-scope.md` -- per `.claude/rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md`, then redeploy. The `.claude/**` path in `file_scope` is declared only so the admission overlap gate can see the collision surface; it is NOT the edit target.

DELIVERABLE HYGIENE. Every edited file is outside `specs/**`, so its prose must carry no task-number references (`.claude/rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md`) and no record-versioning language (`.claude/rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md`). Cite durable anchors only -- file names, function names (`is_contained`), variable names (`files_touched`, `stage_paths`, `run_completeness_check`), section headings, flag names.

PROVENANCE AND CITATION. Raised by /orchestrate's conclusion stage and approved at the lead level as an agent-system change request, session `sess_1791800175_a20f00`. The originating issue-log entry is `entry_id: iss_1791802976646_M8ywmv` in `specs/771_task_reference_lint_debt_boneyard_tests/issues.jsonl` -- `class: scope excursion`, `severity: minor`, `phase: implement`, `dispatch_seq: null`, `resolution: null`, `evidence_path: null`, `suggested_channel: null`. Because that entry carried no `suggested_channel`, the conclusion stage's assignment to the agent-system channel overrode no hint. Note the entry was written BY the defect itself -- `git-commit-phase.sh`'s own `issue-record.sh` call is its author -- so it is a direct machine-generated artifact of the bug rather than a human report of it, and it should be read verbatim before composing anything. RECURRENCE, STATED HONESTLY: a sweep of every `specs/*/issues.jsonl` in this repository finds exactly ONE occurrence of this own-task-dir false-positive class. It is a single observation; what justifies acting on one observation here is not frequency but structure -- the drop is guaranteed to recur on any phase whose self-reported file set is confined to the task's own annotated plan, and the behaviour contradicts two already-written contract texts rather than merely being undesirable.

ADJACENT OBSERVATION -- A DIFFERENT MECHANISM WITH THE OPPOSITE VISIBILITY, RECORDED SO THE GENERAL SHAPE IS VISIBLE. THIS DOES NOT CHANGE THE ONE-OCCURRENCE RECURRENCE BOUND STATED ABOVE, WHICH REMAINS CORRECT FOR THE OWN-TASK-DIR FALSE-POSITIVE CLASS. Task 727 (`stop_literal_null_file_scope_writes_and_promote_check`, completed 2026-10-03) hit a related phase-commit failure, and conflating the two would mis-scope this record.

WHAT HAPPENED THERE. That task carries TWO `task 727: complete implementation` commits, `2af2fe007` and `59c9abb09`. The second is a recovery commit and says so in its own message: the postflight commit failed because the orchestrator tried to stage the source-store copy of `validate-state.sh`, which lives outside this repository; only the in-repo artifacts were committed, and the source-store edits were left uncommitted in the source store by the implementing agent's deliberate choice, to avoid mixing with unrelated dirty state there. The deliverable did eventually land in the source store and is clean there now (the Check 10 `null_value` promotion text is present), but it landed under `78ab8166e`, "meta: promote the literal-null file_scope finding from WARN to FAIL", which names no task. The consequence is that `git log -- agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/validate-state.sh` attributes that file's history to tasks 303, 271, 329 and 279 and to no commit naming 727.

THE THREE WAYS IT DIFFERS, WHICH IS WHY IT IS NOT A SECOND OCCURRENCE OF THE CLASS ABOVE.
  (1) VISIBILITY IS OPPOSITE. The defect this record owns is a SILENT false positive: the path is dropped, the commit succeeds, and the completeness check is disarmed. active_projects.title: Bounded in-file block edits: index and assert, never string-splice
active_projects.description:
Add agent-system guidance for the ASSERTION half of a bounded in-file block edit: assert the expected pre-state before writing, and assert an expected post-state invariant immediately after writing, so that a block edit which goes wrong is caught at once instead of being committed. The ANCHOR-SELECTION half of this same failure class is ALREADY CLAIMED by a sibling record in the source-store repository's own task space -- see the sibling-coverage section below. This record must not restate that half, and is not a licence to rewrite it.

MEASURED, NOT HYPOTHESIZED. A python slice-and-splice edit intended only to flip one phase heading marker and tick that phase's checklist items instead DUPLICATED 773 LINES of a plan file: phases 1 through 9 appeared twice in the result. The mechanism was reconstructing the file by concatenating string slices of its own text; an off-target slice boundary silently re-emitted a region that was already present, and nothing in the write path noticed. The intended change was a handful of characters.

HOW IT WAS CAUGHT, AND WHY THAT IS THE POINT. The duplication was detected IMMEDIATELY by a post-edit `grep -n '^### Phase'` showing 18 phase headings where 9 were expected. The defect was not caught by the edit mechanism, by a diff review, or by reading the file -- it was caught by one cheap assertion on a count that the editor knew in advance. That assertion is the whole lesson, and guidance that omits it is not guidance.

HOW IT WAS RECOVERED, AND A NUANCE THE GUIDANCE MUST STATE EXPLICITLY. The file was restored without loss by rewriting it from `git show HEAD:<path>` and then redoing the edit correctly. THAT RECOVERY IS A PLAIN WRITE, NOT A DESTRUCTIVE GIT OPERATION: `git show` reads a blob to stdout and the restore is an ordinary file write, so the destructive-git guard (`guard-destructive-git.sh`) was never involved and no snapshot was required. State this plainly, because an agent that believes recovery from a botched in-file edit requires `git checkout --`, `git restore`, or `git reset --hard` will either escalate for a permission it does not need or reach for an operation that genuinely is guarded and genuinely would discard its other uncommitted work. The safe recovery path for ONE clobbered file is `git show HEAD:<path>` piped to a write, and it is available on a dirty tree with no guard interaction at all.

WHAT A SIBLING RECORD ALREADY COVERS -- READ IT BEFORE WRITING ANYTHING. The source-store repository (~/.config/nvim) maintains its OWN task space, and a record there already covers the anchor-selection half of this failure class: `lean_phase_commit_full_build_and_plan_anchor` (its ITEM 2), file_scope `agent-system/extensions/lean/context/project/lean4/agents/lean-implementation-flow.md`, `agents/lean-implementation-agent.md`, `agents/lean-implementation-hard-agent.md`. Its incident: a plan-file section splice used the bare string '## Lean Challenge Statements' as its END anchor; that same string also occurs earlier in the file's Goals prose, so the splice matched the earlier occurrence and duplicated 752 lines. Its guidance: a section edit anchors on a LINE beginning with the heading markers and searches FORWARD from the target section's start, never on a bare substring that may recur in prose elsewhere. That record ALSO states explicitly that the failure mode may not be lean-specific at all and that a shared home in the core extension is an acceptable outcome of its own planning, with the lean files pointing at it rather than restating it. THIS RECORD THEREFORE OWNS ONLY THE ASSERTION HALF, and must coordinate with that record on the shared home rather than racing it to create one.

WHY THE ASSERTION HALF IS A GENUINELY SEPARATE ADDITION AND NOT A RESTATEMENT -- THE DECIDING MEASUREMENT. Correct anchor selection would not have prevented either incident on its own, and the two incidents' outcomes differ in exactly the way that proves it. The sibling record's 752-line duplication was COMMITTED: commit 83085ed7e in the consumer repository carries the message "mark phase 14 completed in plan" together with a diff of 752 insertions, and it took a FOLLOW-UP commit, f0ef67f81, to restore the file (19 insertions, 771 deletions). The duplication survived the edit, the commit message, and whatever review that commit received. This record's own 773-line duplication, by contrast, never reached a commit at all, because a post-write `grep -n '^### Phase'` count assertion fired immediately. Same failure class, same magnitude, opposite outcome -- and the only difference in the editing procedure was the presence of one cheap assertion on a count known in advance. An anchor rule makes the mistake rarer; the assertion is what makes it loud. Both halves are needed, which is why neither record should absorb the other silently.

THE DISCIPLINE TO RECORD, IN THREE PARTS, THE THIRD BEING THIS RECORD'S OWN. (1) INDEX, DO NOT SPLICE. Address the edit by line index -- read the file into a list of lines, locate the target block's start and end by matching the lines that delimit it, and replace or rewrite only the lines in that range -- rather than computing character offsets into the file's text and concatenating slices around them. (2) BOUND THE RANGE BY AN EXPLICIT TERMINATOR, AND ASSERT THE PRE-STATE. The originating repair bounded the loop by the NEXT TOP-LEVEL SECTION HEADING rather than by a computed length, and asserted that the located range looked as expected before writing anything -- the marker to be flipped was actually present, the checklist items actually matched, the range actually terminated where a terminator was found rather than at end of file. An edit whose pre-state assertion fails must abort without writing, not proceed on a best guess. HOW THE TERMINATOR ITSELF IS CHOSEN belongs to the sibling record named above -- CITE its heading-line-anchored, search-forward rule, do not restate or re-derive it. (3) ASSERT A POST-STATE INVARIANT IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE WRITE. Pick a property of the whole file that the edit must not change and check it in the same breath as the write -- here, the count of `^### Phase` headings. A structural count is the cheapest and most sensitive such invariant for a sectioned document; a total line count is weaker but still catches gross duplication. Part (3) is THIS RECORD'S distinctive contribution and the one no sibling record covers: parts (1) and (2) make the common failure less likely, part (3) is what makes the uncommon one loud instead of silent.

STATE A TRIGGER CONDITION THE READER CAN CHECK BEFORE ACTING. The guidance must not read as a general prohibition that a reader has to interpret. The trigger is conjunctive: the target is a BOUNDED BLOCK inside a larger line-structured text file (a phase inside a plan, a section inside a document, a record inside a log), AND the mechanism under consideration RECONSTRUCTS the file from string slices of its own content rather than replacing identified lines in place. Both halves must hold. Rewriting a whole file from computed content is not this failure class; neither is a line-indexed in-place replacement, which is the prescribed alternative.

NAME THE FIRST-CHOICE MECHANISM, NOT ONLY THE FALLBACK. The harness `Edit` tool with a unique `old_string` is ITSELF a bounded, assert-on-match edit: it fails loudly when the match is absent or ambiguous, which is precisely the pre-state assertion part (2) asks for, obtained for free. It is the first choice for a small bounded edit and the guidance should say so before describing any scripted path. The scripted, line-indexed path earns its place when the edit is repetitive across many sites in one file, or mechanical enough that enumerating `Edit` calls is impractical -- which is exactly the situation the originating incident was in (one heading marker plus a run of checklist items). Guidance that jumps straight to "write a careful python loop" has skipped the cheaper correct answer.

WHAT THE GUIDANCE MUST NOT SAY. Do not generalize this into "do not use python/scripts to edit files", and do not frame it as "always use the Edit tool" -- both are false and both will be ignored once a reader meets a case they do not fit. Do not present the post-state assertion as optional verification that a careful editor may skip; the originating editor WAS being careful and still shipped a 773-line duplication. Do not restate the destructive-git rules; reference `.claude/rules/git-workflow.md` for those and keep this record's git content to the one `git show HEAD:<path>` recovery nuance above.

BOTH AUDIENCES MUST BE REACHED, AND THEY READ DIFFERENT FILES. (i) An IMPLEMENTER performing the edit needs the mechanism and the assertions. (ii) A PLAN AUTHOR must not author a step phrased as a slice-and-splice reconstruction in the first place. The implementer path is the primary one here -- unlike the jq record this is sequenced behind, the originating defect arose in an implementer's own edit mechanism rather than in a plan step -- so `agents/general-implementation-agent.md`, which already points at sibling core patterns, is the natural referrer and is declared in this record's file_scope. State in the plan which path reaches which audience.

SITING -- THREE RECORDS NOW BEAR ON ONE HOME; READ BOTH NEIGHBOURS BEFORE CREATING A FILE. The shared discipline is claimed, in whole or in part, by this record, by the jq-reserialization record this one is sequenced behind, and by the sibling anchor record in the source-store repository's task space. Creating a new pattern file without reading the other two risks a third competing file about one discipline. Resolution order: (i) read the jq record's landed siting decision -- if it created a new sibling pattern file, ADD a section to that file and widen this record's file_scope to it rather than creating `bounded-block-edit.md`; if it extended `jq-escaping-workarounds.md` instead, create the new file declared in file_scope, because neither a Markdown splice nor an assertion discipline belongs inside a file about jq pitfalls. (ii) Read the sibling anchor record's landed state -- if it has already relocated its ITEM 2 guidance into a core-extension home, that home is THIS record's target too and no new file is warranted; if it has not, this record's file becomes the shared home that record invited, and the lean-side files should POINT at it rather than restate it. In EVERY branch the `index-entries.json` entry and at least one referrer are part of THIS change, not a follow-up -- an unreferenced pattern file is not guidance, it is a file.

SCOPE: GUIDANCE ONLY, NO HELPER SCRIPT. Decided at filing time, for the same reasons the predecessor record records for its own case: the proven mechanism is a short line-indexed loop plus two assertions, and the part that is actual work -- knowing which block this edit targets and which invariant must hold for this file -- cannot be factored into a wrapper. A generic "safe block editor" would need its own test suite, deploy registration and maintenance, out of proportion to one minor, already-recovered incident. REOPEN CONDITION, which the guidance itself should name: if the assertion recipe is being retyped across many tasks, revisit the wrapper question then.

NOTHING IN THE REPOSITORY IS BROKEN. The affected plan file was repaired in the originating run and is correct as it stands; do not re-edit it, and do not treat this record as a data-repair record. This record's entire deliverable is prose in the source store plus its wiring.

ACCEPTANCE. (1) The guidance states the conjunctive trigger condition in terms a reader can check before acting, and names at least one concrete file shape that meets it. (2) It carries a copyable recipe covering all three parts -- line indexing, the bounded range with its pre-state assertion, and the post-write invariant assertion -- not merely a prohibition. (3) It names the `Edit`-tool-with-unique-`old_string` path as the first choice and says when the scripted path earns its place instead. (4) It states the `git show HEAD:<path>` recovery nuance, including that this is a plain write with no destructive-git-guard interaction, and does not restate the guard's own rules. (5) It does not generalize into a prohibition on scripted editing. (6) A reader arriving from the predecessor record's guidance, or from `agents/general-implementation-agent.md`, reaches this guidance without knowing the term "slice-and-splice" in advance. (7) The new or extended file carries an `index-entries.json` entry whose `line_count` and `keywords` agree with the file as landed, plus at least one referrer. (8) `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` reports `RESULT=landed_verify_clean` afterwards.

IF A NEW FILE PATH IS CHOSEN THAT IS NOT ALREADY IN file_scope, WIDEN file_scope FIRST. Add the path through `update-task-status.sh` rather than writing into a file_scope-unlisted location silently. This applies in particular to siting branch (a), where the predecessor's file becomes this record's edit target.

SOURCE-STORE BOUNDARY. `.claude/**` is a gitignored, regenerated deploy artifact; a hand edit there is wiped by the next deploy and will appear to succeed while having no lasting effect. Resolve `source_dir` from `<project-root>/.claude-extensions.json` for the owning extension (`core`, whose source store is `/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core`) and edit at the mirroring path there, per `.claude/rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md`. Then redeploy via `bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh` and confirm `RESULT=landed_verify_clean`. The `.claude/**` paths in file_scope are declared only so the admission overlap gate can see the collision surface; they are NOT the edit target.

DELIVERABLE HYGIENE. Every edited file lies outside `specs/**`, so its prose must carry no task-number references (`.claude/rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md`) and no record-versioning language (`.claude/rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md`). The tool names, the `grep` pattern, the rule filenames and the guard script name are durable anchors and may be cited; the originating task number and the issue entry_id may NOT appear in the guidance prose -- they live in this record only. Describe the discipline as what an editor does, never as a narration of a past incident's draft history.

PROVENANCE. Raised during orchestration of the sliced-certificate LiveAt nontermination work and approved at the lead level as an agent-system change request. The originating issue-log entry is in `specs/716_sliced_certificate_liveat_nontermination/issues.jsonl`, entry_id `iss_1791939778284_8Gc4jM` -- class `tooling`, severity `minor`, phase `implement`, dispatch_seq 11. The entry carried NO `suggested_channel` hint, so there is no hint-versus-decision override to state: the orchestrate lead classified it to the agent-system channel on its own judgment, on the ground that the remedy is agent-system guidance rather than repository work product. The technique is not Lean-specific and is deliberately sited in the `core` extension rather than the `lean` one.

DEPENDENCY RATIONALE, AND WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE RECORD RATHER THAN A FOLD. The declared edge on the jq-reserialization record serializes a genuine file overlap -- both records touch `agent-system/extensions/core/index-entries.json` and `agent-system/extensions/core/merge-sources/claudemd.md`, and in one siting branch they touch the same pattern file -- and it also sequences the siting decision above, which cannot be made correctly before the predecessor lands. It is filed SEPARATELY rather than folded into that record because the two trigger conditions are genuinely different and a reader checks them separately: that record keys on a formatting-sensitive JSON file plus `jq`'s lack of a preserving mode, this one keys on a bounded block inside a line-structured text file plus a string-slice mechanism. That record also carries an explicit, reasoned boundary around what its guidance must not claim, and folding a second, differently-triggered defect into it would reopen settled scope decisions. The shared abstraction is handled by siting them together, which the edge makes possible, rather than by merging the two records. CROSS-REPO HAZARD, AND WHY NO EDGE EXPRESSES IT. The sibling anchor record lives in a DIFFERENT repository's task space from this one, so no dependency edge and no file_scope overlap gate can span the two -- both task systems file records against the same source store under `agent-system/extensions/**`, and neither can see the other's claims. The coordination above is therefore a manual read, stated here because nothing mechanical will enforce it. Whoever implements this record must check the sibling's state by hand first.

RELATED RECORDS, FOR ORIENTATION ONLY -- NO FURTHER DEPENDENCY EDGES. `agent-system/extensions/core/agents/planner-agent.md` is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from this record's file_scope even though the plan-author audience makes it a tempting referrer: the plan-format blocked-decision-gate record already claims that path, and the jq record excluded it on the same ground. If research concludes a matching line in `planner-agent.md` is genuinely necessary, add a serializing dependency edge at that point (`update-task-status.sh --depends-on-add`) rather than editing a file another record claims.

FROZEN-RECORD TRACKER. Seven task records in this repository cannot be worked here and must not be dispatched: 730, 741, 752, 767, 768, 769, 770.

WHY THEY ARE FROZEN. Each names an edit target that resolves only under the agent-system source store. Resolve it the usual way: source_dir in <project-root>/.claude-extensions.json points at /home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/** (a core entry plus a sibling lean entry). This repository carries only the deployed .claude/ tree, which is a disposable artifact regenerated from that store (rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). A dispatch picking up any of the seven from here can read nothing it is meant to edit and can commit nothing it manages to write; an edit that did land under .claude/** would be wiped by the next deploy.

WHERE THE REAL WORK IS TRACKED. The agent-system source store carries its own migration record covering exactly these seven (it was numbered 390 there on 2026-10-13, topic orchestrator; re-resolve by description rather than trusting that number, since the other repo renumbers on vault operations). That record owns the transplant: moving the seven into the source store's task space and renumbering them from its counter. It also settles that 752 is to be MIGRATED, not abandoned -- an earlier reading treated it as already fixed by a completed source-store record, and that reading was wrong.

THIS RECORD'S OWN DELIVERABLE (the part this repository owns). Once the migration has landed:
1. VERIFY FIRST, then delete. Confirm each of the seven exists in the source store's task space before removing anything here. Never delete an unverified record -- a half-finished migration plus a deletion here loses the task outright.
2. Remove the seven from specs/state.json's active_projects via state-write.sh (never a hand edit), then regenerate specs/TODO.md with generate-todo.sh.
3. Drop the second paragraph of specs/ROADMAP.md's "Not batched, and why" section (the one naming 730, 741, 752, 767, 768, 769, 770). Leave the first paragraph, which covers the Stage 0 ruling holds, intact.
4. Close this record.

GUARDRAILS.
(a) Do NOT attempt any of the seven tasks' underlying work from this repository, however small it looks -- that is the entire reason they are frozen.
(b) Do NOT re-add them to an /orchestrate batch line in specs/ROADMAP.md. They were removed from four Stage 3 lines on 2026-10-13 precisely because batching them dispatches work that cannot complete.
(c) 768 in particular must be re-read live before any implementation: part of its third defect (the list-item Goals range anchor and the reserved-keyword denylist) is ALREADY LANDED AND COMMITTED in the lean source store at 42c23f442, suite 16/16 green.
